OCT. 1 (AP)-I WAS QUT FOR A WALK IN MOSCOW ONE 
AUTUMN NIGHT A FEW YEARS AGOe MY MEDIATIONS WERE INTERRUPTED BY A 
ROAR AND A CRASH. ACROSS THE STREET A CLOUDY OF DUST AND PLASTER 
AROSE. PEOPLE RAN FROM ALL DIRECTIONS. 

IT WAS EASY TO SEE WHAT HAD HAPPENED. A FINE SOVIET BUILDING-- 
FINE BY SOVIET STANDARDS--STOOD OPPOSITE ME. THREE FLOORS UP THERE 
USED TO BE A BALCONY. THE BALCONY HAD SIMPLY FALLEN OFF THE 
FRONT OF THE BUILDING. ) 

ONE DOES NOT HAVE TO BE AN EXPERT TO REALIZE THAT MOST OF THE BUIL 
DINGS ARE POORLY CONSTRUCTED AND THAT ALMOST THE WHOLE CONSTRUCTION 
INDUSTRY IS INEFFICIENT AND ANTIQUATED. YOU CAN SEE THIS IN WATCHING 
NEW BUILDINGS GO UP. OR YOU CAN WALK UP TO AN OLDER BUILDING AND 
START GUESSING WHEN IT WAS BUILT. AN AMERICAN MIGHT GUESS 50 YEARS3,. 
THE CORNERSTONE WILL SHOW IT WAS ERECTED 3 OR MAYBE 15 YEARS AGO. @pT 
IT ALREADY LOOKS OLD. THE WORK WAS POOR. THE BUILDING IS DIRTY. | 

SOME BUILDINGS IN MOSCOW LOOK YEARS OLD EVEN BEFORE THEY ARE FINISHED 

MOST ARE BUILT OF BRICK. BUT THE BUILDERS DO NOT HAVE FACING BRICK. 


| INSEAD THEY COVER OVER THE SURFACE WITH PLASTER. 


' FACING BUT NEVER GOT IT. 
* TEND TO PUT A 


{ 


THE PLASTER SOMETIMES STARTS FALLING OFF BEFORE THE BUILDING IS 
EVEN FINISHED. EVEN WHEN IT STAYS ON IT DOES NOT LOOK GOOD. IT IS 
USUALLY PAINTED WITH SOME SORT OF PLASTER PAINT -- OFTEN IN A PASTEL 
SHADEe THIS SURFACE COLLECTS THE DIRT. WITHIN A FEW MONTHS IT LOOKS 


BAD. 
THERE ARE MANY BRICK BUILDINGS WHICH WERE INTENDED TO HAVE A PLASTER 
THEY LOOK EVEN WORSE.

SOVIET ARCHITECTURAL DESIGN IS NOT GENERALLY GOOD. 
ORNATE DECORATION -- GINGERBREAD -- ON BUILDINGS.

KUALA—LUMPUR, MALAYA, OCT. 1 (AP)-INVESTMENT CIRCLES REPORTEED TODAY 
THAT EUROPEAN OWNERS SINCE 1951 HAVE SOLD 85.000 ACRES OF RUBBER 
ESTATES TO CHINESE BECAUSE OF COMMUNIST TERRORIST ACTIVITY. 

THE SOURCES ADDED, HOWEVER, THAT MOST OF THE CAPITAL REALIZED -- 
ABOUT 26 MILLION Us S. DOLLARS -- WAS BEING KEPT IN MALAYA FOR 
REINVESTMENT WHEN BRITAIN WINS HER WAR AGAINST CHINESE COMMUNIST 
GUERRILAS PLAGUING THE PENINSULA. 

IN A FEW CASES COMPANIES OPERATING THE ESTATES WERE CLOSED DOWN 
AND MONEY REALIZED FROM THE SALES WAS DISTRIBUTED TO STOCKHOLDERS. 
__A TOTAL OF 41 ESTATES REPORTEDLY CHANGED HANDS. BUSINESS SOURCES 
SAID MUCH OF THE ACREAGE WAS PLANTED IN OLD RUBBER NEARING THE END OF 
ITS PRODUCTIVE LIFE.

WASHINGTON, OCT. 1 (AP)-AMERICANS -- AND RUSSIANS -- MAY GET FROM

THE UNITED STATES SHATTERED A PACIFIC TSLAND WITH 4A HYDROGEN EXPLOS- 


ION. 

THAT POSSIBILITY IS SUGGESTED BY EISENHOWER'S STATEMENT YESTERDAY 
THAT HE [IS SORTING OUT IN HIS MIND WHAT HE SHOULD SAY IN A PROPOSED 
a DISCUSSION OF WORLD TENSION AND GROWING DESTRUCTIVENESS OF 

TO PRESENT AS PART OF THAT BROAD DISCUSSION A PICTURE OF THE DIS- 
ASTER THAT WOULD COME TO ALL NATIONS IN AN H-BOMB WAR, THE PRESIDENT 
MAY FEEL IMPELLED TO TELL WHAT THE NEWEST AND MOST DREADFUL WEAPON IN 
THE ARSENAL CAN DO--IF USED BY EITHER THE UNITED STATES OR RUSSI4e 

PERSONAL LETTERS WRITTEN BY MEN WHO WITNESSED AN UNPRECEDENTED 
EXPLOSION AT ENIWETOK LAST FALL TOLD OF A WHOLE ISLAND OF THE 
PACIFIC ATOLL DISAPPEARING IN THE BLAST. 

UNTIL LAST NIGHT THE ATOMIC ENERGY COMMISSION \AEC) HAD NOT 
EVEN CONCEDED THAT AN ACTUAL HYDROGEN BLAST OCCURRED AT -ENIWETOK. IT 
HAD SPOKEN GUARDEDLY OF EXPERIMENTS “CONTRIBUTING TO THERMONUCLEAR 
RESEARCH. 

BUT IN AN ADDRESS LAST NIGHT AT NEW YORK, AEC CHAIRMAN LEWIS 
Le STRAUSS REFERRED TO THE TEST OF A " THERMONUCLEAR DEVICE.” IN 
THE LANGUAGE OF ATOMIC EXPERTS A *DEVICE® CAN PRODUCE ALL THE POWER 
AND OTHER FEATURES OF AN ACTUAL WEAPON. THE ONLY DIFFERENCE IS THAT 
IT IS ENCUMBERED AND FESTOONED WITH RECORDING INSTRUMENTS AND IS 
NOT NECESSARILY FITTED INTO THE BALLISTICS-PERFECT CONTAINER OF 4 
BOMB OR PROJECTILE. 

EISENHOWER MUST WEIGH WHAT HE CAN SAY ABOUT THE POWER OF THE 
HYDROGEN WEAPON AND STILL KEEP SECRET IMPORTANT TECHNICAL DATA. 

RUSSIA HAS SAID--AND THE UNITED STATES HAS CONFIRMED--THAT THE 
SOVIETS SUCCEEDED IN PRODUCING A HYDROGEN EXPLOSION. TO THIS STRAUSS 
ADDED THE OMINOUS WORD THAT HE BELIEVES THE SOVIET UNION STARTED 
DEVELOPMENT OF THE HYDROGEN BOMB SOME TIME BEFORE THE UNITED STATES. 
HE BLAMED ESPIONAGE AND *TREASON® FOR THE ABILITY OF THE RUSSIANS TO 
phi} yg A HYDROGEN BLAST WITHIN NINE MONTHS AFTER THE UNITED 

THIS IN TURN FOLLOWS INFORMATION FROM WELL INFORMED SOURCES THAT 
A NEW TECHNIQUE FOR FIRING A HYDROGEN BOMB, NOT REQUIRING USE OF 
A STANDARD ATOMIC BOMB AS -THE TRIGGER, MAY BE AN IMPORTANT FACTOR 
IN MAKING THE HYDROGEN WEAPON RELATIVELY CHEAP AND EASY TO BUILD 
FOR MANY NATIONS WITHIN FRWSYEARS.

DEFENSE AND THE IMPACT ON THE NATION'S MILITARY BUDGET. 

IF EVEN ONE SOVIET PLANE WITH ONE HYDROGEN BOMB GOT THROUGH THE 
AIR DEFENSE SYSTEM, A BIG AMERICAN CITY COULD BE VAPORIZED. AND 
SAY UNITED STATES AIR FORCE OFFICIALS, THE MONEY REQUIRED TO BUILD A

(ADVANCE) NBSW-YORK, OCT. 1 (AP)-DEAN ACHESON GRAVELY COUNSELED THE 
UNITED STATES TONIGHT TO SHUN ANY ACT AT HOME OR ABROAD THAT MIGHT 
WEAKEN THE COALITION OF FREE NATIONS.» 

THE DEMOCRATIC FORMER SECRETARY OF STATE, WHO SPOKE AT A DINNER 
OF THE WOODROW WILSON FOUNDATION IN THE WALDORF-ASTORIA HOTEL, 
DIVIDED THE POSTWAR YEARS INTO TWO PHASES: 
OF THE WESTERN COALITION AMID CONFUSION AND EVIDENT 

2. "MAINTENANCE AND MANAGEMENT OF THE COALITION AGAINST CAJOLERY 
AND SUBVERSION IN THE FACE OF A MORE HIDDEN BUT PERHAPS GREATER DANGER." 

WHILE THE COALITION WAS BEING CREATED, ACHESON SAID. THE RUSSIANS 
FAILED TO WIN "THE VITAL INDUSTRIAL CENTERS OF EUROPE TO COMPLEMENT 
THEIR SYSTEM.” HOWEVER, THEY WON "THE UNDEVELOPED AREA OF CHINA cAND) 
THEIR GAIN HERE WAS Logs FOR US." 

ACHESON SAID THAT IN THE CURRENT PHASE, NEGOTIATION WITH THE 
COMMUNISTS "IS POSSIBLE, IS DESIRABLE AND MAY--BUT ONLY MAY--BE 
PRODUCTIVE. « »« BUT NEGOTIATION IS A METHOD, NOT AN END OF POLICY." 

THE CENTRAL POINT OF FOREIGN POLICY, HE WENT ON, “IS THE HEALTH AND 
STRENGTH AND COHESIVENESS OF OUR COALITION.® 

HE SAID THE LEADER OF THE COALITION OF FREE PEOPLES CANNOT HAVE 
"PERSONAL OR NARROW" INTERESTS OR "YIELD TO THE DEMANDS OF DOMESTIC 


POLITICS." 
HE WAS PRESENTED THE FOUNDATION'S AWARD, A BRONZE PLAQUE GIVEN FROM 


TIME TO TIME FOR “MERITORIOUS SERVICE TO DEMOCRACY, PUBLIC WELFA 
LIBERAL THOUGHT OR PEACE THROUGH JUSTICE." 


THE FOUNDATION WAS SET UP THROUGH PUBLIC SUBSCRIPTION IN 1922 To 
PERPETUATE WOODROW WILSON'S IDEAS OF WORLD ORGANIZATION AND 3 
INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION.

SENIOR OFFICERS IN THE ARMED SERVICES, AND OF MILITARIZED AND SEMI- 
MILITARIZED ORGANIZATIONS SUCH AS THE POLICE. : 

THEREARE HIGH RANKING INDUSTRIAL AND ECONOMIC EXECUTIVES SCIENTISTS 

AND RESEARCH MEN. THERE ARE RESPONSIBLE GOVERNMENT AND PARTY OFFICIALS, 
AND SUCCESSFUL PEOPLE FROM THE LITERARY AND ARTISTIC WORLD. A CERTAIN 
NUMBER OF TECHNICIANS AND WORKERS, FOR REASON OF SPECIAL SKILLS OR 

WORK IN PARTICULAR REGIONS, BENEFIT FROM SPECIAL BONUS PAYMENT SCHEMES. 
CERTAIN COLLECTIVE FARM EXECUTIVES AND FARMERS BENEFIT FROM SPECIAL BONU 
SCHEMES -FOR PARTICULAR CROPS. FINALLY, SOME DOCTORS AND OTHER 
PROFESSIONAL MEN HAVE LUCRATIVE PRIVATE PRACTICE.

IN MOSCOW STORES, TO BUY ONE SMALL PIECE OF FOODSTUFF OR 
MERCHANDISE ONE HAS TO LINE UP THREE TIMES. THE FIRST TIME. TO GET 
NEAR THE COUNTER SO AS TO SEE THE PRICE AND WHETHER AN ARTICLE TS 
AVAILABLE. THE SECOND TIME, TO PAY THE CASHIER. THE THIRD TIME, TO 
RECEIVE WHAT ONE HAS PURCHASED. BEFORE ONE HAS PURCHASED GROCESIES For 
THE DAY IN THE GASTRONOME, ONE MAY HAVE BEEN IN 15 DIFFERENT LINES. 

THIS INEFFICIENCY GOES ON EVERY HOUR IN THE CAPITAL OF THE SECOND 
GREATEST INDUSTRIAL POWER ON THE EARTH. 

THERE IS NO PAT OR SIMPLE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION OF HOW EFFICIENT

FLOOD OF PROPAGANDA ON THE VIRTUES OF THE COMMUNIST WAY OF LIFE.

MARGATE: ENGLAND, OCTe 3 (AP)-THE LABOR PARTY HAS ABANDONED ITS 
TRADITIONAL SOCIALIST BELIEF THAT STATE OWNERSHIP OF ALL INDUSTRY 
WOULD BRING ON A WORKERS" PARADISE. 

INSTEAD, THE DISSENSION-RIDDEN PARTY DECIDED AT A CONFERENCE 
HERE THIS WEEK TO WORK FOR A WELFARE STATE. 

EVERYONE AGREED ON SUCH THINGS AS LARGER OLD AGE PENSIONS AND SICK 
BENEFITS AND BETTER TAX-SUPPORTED SCHOOLS. BUT THE MANUAL WORKERS' 
DELEGATES KILLED LEFTIST PROPOSALS FOR WHOLESALE NATIONALIZATION OF 
INDUSTRY AND OF LAND. 

IF THE ATTITUDE OF THE TRADE UNION LEADERS IS AN ACCURATE 
REFLECTION OF RANK-AND-FILE SENTIMENT, GREAT NUMBERS OF WORKERS 
WITH CLOTH CAPS AND TOIL-WORN HANDS HAVE LOST THEIR BELIEF IN STATE 
OWNERSHIP IN THE YEARS SINCE WORLD WAR IT. 

LEFTIST ANEURIN BEVAN THUNDERED THAT THE CAUTIOUS ATTITUDE OF THE 
UNIONS CONSTITUTED "TREASON TO THE SPIRIT OF SOCIALISM. 

BUT THE BIG UNION LEADERS AND THE HUMBLE MEMBERS OF THE UNION 
DELEGATIONS HAD AN ANSWER FOR THAT. A BENT LITTLE COAL MINER NAMED 
HARRY ELLISON TOLD THE LEFTWINGERS: 

“A BOSS IS A BOSS, NO MATTER WHETHER HE GETS THE JOB FROM THE 
STATE OR PRIVATE OWNERS. SOMETIMES THE BOSSES OF PRIVATE INDUSTRY 
ARE MORE REASONABLE TO DEAL WITH."

mr LONDON OCT 3 (AP)-BRITAIN REPORTEDLY IS PUSHING A PLAN AIMED AT 


BREAKING THE KOREAN PEACE CONFERENCE DEADLOCK BY LETTING BOTH SIDES 
ONVITE CERTAIN NEUTRALS, INCLUDING INDIA, TO JOIN THE DELIBERATIONS. 

MINISTER OF STATE SELWYN LLOYD, WHO HAS BEEN WORKING WITH THE UNITE 
STATES AND OTHER UNITED NATIONS MEMBERS IN AN EFFORT TO GET THE KOREAN 
PARLEY STARTED BY OCT. 28, WAS EXPECTED TO ARRIVE BY PLANE TODAY FROM 
NEW YORK TO CONFER WITH FOREIGN SECRETARY ANTHONY EDEN. 

LLOYD WAS SUMMONED YESTERDAY AFTER DIPLOMATIC INFORMANTS SAID THE 
CHURCHILL CABINET HAD WORKED OUT THE NEW KOREAN STRATEGY. 

ALTHOUGH NO OFFICIAL DETAILS WERE AVAILABLE ON THE PLAN, THE 
INFORMANTS SAID IT WAS BASED ON THE ASSUMPTION THAT THE PROPOSED 
KOREAN PEACE PARLEY WILL HAVE TO BE BROADENED. | 

IT PROPOSES, THEY SAID, THAT THE PEACE CONFERENCE AS A WHOLE--THE 
COMMUNIST SIDE’AS WELL AS THE UsNe SIDE--NOW AGREE TO INVITE NEUTRALS 
To JOIN IN THE TALKS: THE UeSe HAS AGREED THE CONFERENCE ITSELF 
COULD INVITE OUTSIDERS--BUT ONLY AFTER IT BEGINS ITS DELIBERATIONS. 
THE RUSSIANS HAVE WARNED THE CONFERENCE MAY NEVER TAKE PLACE UNLESS 


THE Ue» ADOPTS THEIR PROPO 


THE UsNe ADOPTS THEIR PROPOSAL THAT CERTAIN ASIAN NATIONS--SUCH AS 
INDIA, BURMA AND PAKISTAN--SIT 

THE UsNe MAJORITY VOTED AGAINST THIS PROPOSAL, SUPPORTING THE UsS~ 
CONTENTION THAT THE ARMISTICE TERMS CONFINED THE CONFERENCE AT THE 
START TO THOSE COUNTRIES WHICH FOUGHT IN KOREA. 

THE DIPLOMATIC INFORMANTS SAID THE BRITISH “UNDERSTAND” THE UNITED 
STATES IS PREPARED TO GO ALONG WITH THE NEW IDEA, ALTHOUGH NO 
FORMAL AGREEMENT HAS BEEN REACHED.

CLASSES MASS DESTRUCTION OF PEOPLE BECAUSE OF RACE, CULTURE OR COLOR AS 
\ CRIME AGAINST HUMANITY. IT ALSO COVERS SLAVE LABOR. BUT SECRETARY

THE UNITED STATES HAD TWO REPRESENTATIVES SITTING IN RECENT SESSIONS

FINALLY DECIDED TO HAVE ONE. THE QUESTION WILL NOT COME BEFORE THE 
ASSEMBLY BEFORE NEXT YEAR. 

THE DRAFT CODE FINALLY APPROVED BY THE COMMISSION EXPERTS WOULD 
PROVIDE THAT ANY COUNTRY ACCEPTING THE IDEA OF THE COURT WOULD HAVE 
TO RATIFY IT BEFORE IT AFFECTED THE COUNTRY. A 15-JUDGE BENCH WAS PRO- 
POSED TO TRY CRIMES UNDER INTERNATIONAL LAW. INDIVIDUALS, WHETHER 
RULERS, PUBLIC OFFICIALS OR PRIVATE INDIVIDUALS, WOULD BE’ LIABLE TO 
PROSECUTION BEFORE THE COURT. THE DRAFT CODE, HOWEVER, DID NOT SPELL 
OUT THE NATURE OF THE CRIMES. THEIR DEFINITION WOULD BE LEFT TO FUTURE 
INTERNATIONAL CONVENTIONS TO BE RATIFIED BY INDIVIDUAL COUNTRIES, AS

NEW DELHIy OCT 3 -(AP)=INDIA HOPES TO BLUNT THE SHARP EDGE OF: ITS 
STAGGERING UNEMPLOYMENT PROBLEM WITH A NEW GOVERNMENT PROGRAM. 

EIGHTY THOUSAND COLLEGE GRADUATES WHO SPEND THEIR DAYS SNIPING AT 
THE GOVERNMENT FROM COFFEE HOUSE CHAIRS WILL RECEIVE TEACHING JOBS 
UNDER THE CENTRAL EDUCATION MINISTRY*S RURAL SCHOOL EXPANSION DRIVE. 

PREMIER NEHRU HAS PUSHED THIS STOP=GAP PROGRAM--A SMALL BUT 
IMPORTANT START IN SLASHING AN ESTIMATED TOTAL OF ONE MILLION EDUCATED 
JNEMPLOYED -- TO CHECK A GROWING DRIFT OF IDLE YOUNG INTELLECTUALS 
INTO WAITING COMMUNIST ARMS. 

EDUCATION MINISTRY OFFICIALS PLAN TO PUT 30,000 YOUTHS THROUGH SIX- 
JEEK TRAINING COURSES DURING THE NEXT YEAR AND 50,000 MORE BY 1955. . 
TRAINEES WILL CET ASSIGNMENTS IN VILLAGE AREAS WHERE NO SCHOOLS EXIST 

FOR MOST OF THE YOUTHS ENTERING THE PLAN, VILLAGE SCHOOL-TEACHING 
IS A FAR CRY FROM THE "RESPECTABLE" WHITE-COLLAR EMPLOYMENT THEY WOULD 
SATHER FIND IN MORE COMFORTABLE BIG CITY GOVERNMENT OR BUSINESS

ATOMIC SECRETS BUDGET (450) 
BY JACK BELL 

WASHINGTON, OCT. 4 (AP)-SEN« HICKENLOOPER (R-LOWA) SAID TODAY THERE 
MAY BE MORE DANGER THAN BENEFIT IN ANY MOVE TO TELL THE AMERICAN PEOPLE 
MORE THAN THEY ALREADY KNOW ABOUT ATOMIC AND HYDROGEN 80MB DEVELOP- 

AS THE TOP REPUBLICAN SENATOR ON THE SENATE-HOUSE ATOMIC ENERGY 
COMMITTEE, HICKENLOOPER THUS TOOK ISSUE WITH SOME OTHER ADMINISTRATION 
OFFICIALS WHO HAVE BEEN URGING PRESIDENT EISENHOWER TO LET THE PUBLIC 
IN ON MORE ATOMIC SECRETS. 

"THE AMERICAN PEOPLE HAVE BEEN GIVEN THE FUNDAMENTAL FACTS OF 
THE TREMENDOUS POWER OF ATOMIC WEAPONS,” HICKENLOOER SAID IN AN INTER- 
VIEW. "I DON'T KNOW MUCH MORE THAT COULD BE SAID WITHOUT GOING INTO 
TECHNICAL DATA WHICH WOULD BENEFIT OUR ENEMIES. 

"CERTAINLY ANY ACTION TO REVEAL THE EXTENT OF OUR STOCKPILING OF 
BOMBS WOULD BE OF GREAT SERVICE TO OUR ENEMIES." 

EISENHOWER TOLD A WHITE HOUSE NEWS CONFERENCE LAST WEDNESDAY THAT 
WHEN HE HAS TIME TO SORT OUT IN HIS OWN MIND HOW TO APPROACH THE 
SUBJECT HE INTENDS TO BE VERY FRANK IN TELLING THE PEOPLE 
THE CONCLUSIONS HE HAS REACHED ON THE RELATIONSHIP OF WORLD TENSIONS 
TO THE GROWING DESTRUCTIVENESS OF ARMAMENTS, 

THE PRESIDENT ADDED, PERHAPS SIGNIFICANTLY, THAT FRIGHTENED 
PEOPLE CANNOT MAKE GOOD DECISIONS, AND THIS COUNTRY DIDN'T WANT To 
FRIGHTEN ANYONE TO DEATH IN THIS WORLD.

419WX 

THE VIEWS HICKENLOOPER EXPRESSED TODAY WERE IN SHARP CONTRAST

THULE, WITH A 10,)000-FOOT RUNWAY, IS NOW FULLY OPERATIONAL AFTER 
THREE YEARS OF INTENSIVE CONSTRUCTION. SPECIAL FUEL FACILITIES FOR 
GASSING UP QUICKLY A WHOLE UNIT OF THE GIANT HEAVY BOMBERS, WHICH 
USE BOTH STANDARD AND JET FUEL, ARE PROVIDED. OF NINE HANGARS AT THE 
ARCTIC AIRFIELD, SIX CAN ACCOMMODATE THE 230-FOOT WINGSPREAD OF THE 
B56S IF THEY NEED REPAIRS OR OTHER SERVICE WHICH CAN NOT BE DONE 

WHEN THE EXTREME COLD (50 OR 60 DEGREES BELOW ZERO) CLOSES IN ON 
THULE THE ENGINES OF THE AIRCRAFT PARKED IN THE OPEN ARE STARTED UP 
PERIODICALLY TO PREVENT "COLD SOAK" WHICH CHILLS METAL TO BRITTLENESS, 
CONGEALS EVEN WINTEREZED LUBIRANTS AND PRODUCES IGNITION TROUBLE.

GALLIPOLI, TURKISH THRACE, OCT. 5 (AP)-THIS HISTORIC, STRATEGIC 
DARDENELLES PORT WAS THREATENED TODAY BY "INVADERS FROM BEHIND THE TRON 
URTAINe 

BUT THE TURKISH FIRST ARMY TURNED THE "INVADERS" BACK AFTER THEY 
HAD DRIVEN TO WITHIN A COUPLE OF MILES OF THIS STRAITS TOWN, MADE 
FAMOUS BY THE BATTLE BETWEEN BRITISH AND TURKS IN 1915 

WITH THE HELP OF A "LOST" GREEK BATTALION, THE TURKS LAUNCHED A 
COUNTER-OFFENSIVE AIMED AT THROWING THE "ENEMY" BACK WHERE THEY 
SUPPOSEDLY CAME FROM--COMMUNIST BULGARIA. 

IT WAS A MAKE-BELIEVE BATTLE, PART OF NATO'S OPERATION WELDFAST Now 
UNDERWAY IN THE MEDITERRANEANs BUT TURKISH OFFICERS, EXTOLLING THEIR 
TROOPS, DID NOT LET THEM FORGET WHO THE REAL ENEMY [S. 

ALWAYS REMEMBER THAT THE ENEMY ARE THE RUSSIANS AND MAYBE LATER 
THE BULGARIANS," GEN. NURETTIN BARANSEL, HARD-BITTEN COMMANDING 
GENERAL OF THE TURKISH FIRST ARMY, SAID TO HIS FORCE. 

THE BATTLE IN SOUTHERN TURKISH THRACE WAS AIMED AT TESTING TURKISH 
DEFENSES OF GALLIPOLI AND THE IMPORTANT STRAITS OF THE DARDENELLFS-— 

4 CERTAIN RED ARMY OBJECTIVE IN THE EVENT OF WAR. 

THE AREA AROUND GALLIPOLI, WHERE NO FOREIGN SHIPS ARE ALLOWED To 

ENTER, IS ENTIRELY RESTRICTED. AFTER CONSIDERABLE TALKING, TURKISH 
TLITARY AUTHORITIES AGREED TO BRIEF VISITS 3Y NEWSPAPERMEN COVERING 

THE DUSTY ROAD WINDING OVER THE RANGE OF LOW HILLS FROM THE INTERIOR 
OF THRACE TO GALLIPOLI BRISTLES WITH DEFENSE WORKS. CONCRETE 
BLOCKHOUSES ARE SPOTTED AT REGULAR INTERVALS ALONG THE BUMPY ROAD. 
GUNS POINTING TOWARD THE SEA JUT OUT OF CONCRETE BASTIONS BUILT IN THE 
SIDE OF THE HILLS. TANK TRAPS CAN BE SEEN EVERY FEW MILFS. 

GALLIPOLI, WHICH FEW FOREIGNERS ARE ALLOWED TO VISIT, IS ITSELF AN 
ORDINARY TURKISH CITY ON THE HEADLAND WITH COBBLED STREZTS AND AN 
ASSORTMENT OF ANCIENT DRAB BUILDINGS SIDE BY SIDE WITH MODERN WESTERN 


TYPE STRUCTURES.

BY JOHN Me HIGHTOWER 

WASHINGTON, OCT. 5 (AP)-SOME TOP UeS. POLICY MAKERS BELIEVE THE 
UNITED STATES AND RUSSIA ARE APPROACHING AN ATOMIC STALEMATE. 

SOME THINK THIS MAY TEND TO STABILIZE RELATIONSHIPS OF THE BIG 
POWERS AND SO CONTRIBUTE TO DEVELOPMENT OF MORE PEACEFUL RELATIONS, 


HOWEVER UNEASY. 

AT THE SAME TIME, FOREIGN POLICY EXPERTS BELIEVE A SITUATION APPROACH 
ING A DIPLOMATIC STALEMATE, PERHAPS INFLUENCED BY THE SHIFTING MILITARY 
POWER BALANCE BUT MORE LIKELY BY OTHER FACTORS, IS ALREADY AT HANDs 

STATE DEPARTMENT OFFICIALS GENERALLY BELIEVE THE SOVIETS ARE ACTIVE- 
LY AVOIDING ANY REAL NEGOTIATIONS CONCERNING GERMANY NOW AND WILL DO So 
FOR MANY MONTHS TO COME. THEY QUESTION WHETHER THE REDS WANT TO TALK 
SERIOUSLY ABOUT THE FAR EAST, ALTHOUGH THEIR POSITION IS RELATIVELY 
STRONGER THERE. 

THE COMBINATION OF AN ATOMIC STALEMATE, IF IT BECOMES AN ACCEPTED 
FACT IN GREAT POWER POLICIES, AND A DIPLOMATIC STANDOFF MIGHT VERY WELL 
FREEZE THE PRESENT STATE OF RELATIONSHIPS INDEFINITELY EVEN WITHOUT 
ANY FORMAL EAST-WEST AGREEMENTS TO THAT EFFECT« 


oat "ds MFSSED BUTTONS THEREBY CUTTING OFF THE MICROPHONES AND THE 2 


THE ESSENCE OF THE ATOMIC BALANCE IS SIMPLE. WITH ITS REPORTED 
MASTERY OF A HYDROGEN EXPLOSION AND ITS ESTABLISHED ATOMIC PROGRESS 
RUSSIA IS CLOSE TO THE POINT OF ACHIEVING A KIND OF BALANCE WITH THE 
UNITED STATES. 

MOST ESTIMATES ARE THAT THE UNITED STATES RETAINS A SIZEABLE MARGIN 
IN THE NUMBER OF BOMBS STOCKPILED. BUT THE DESTRUCTIVE 
POWER OF THE BIG BOMBS IS SO GREAT THAT EQUALITY OF NUMBERS [S_ NOT 
THE KEY TO THEIR EFFECT ON MILITARY STRATEGY. THE KEY IS THE NUMBER 
REQUIRED TO DO A DEVASTATING AMOUNT OF DAMAGE. 

THE SPREADING IDEA THAT AN ATOMIC STALEMATE IS APPROACHING STEMS . 
FROM THE ESTIMATE THAT THE UNITED STATES AND RUSSIA WILL SOON BE ABLE 


TO DO DEVASTATING INJURY TO EACH OTHER. AQd\ 


Anu tS COUNTRY, OF COURSE, HAS HAD THE POWER TO WORK ATOMIC DESTRUC- 
TION ON THE SOVIET UNION FOR SEVERAL YEARS. THIS IS BELIEVED BY MANY 
To HAVE BEEN THE MAIN REASON WHY THE SOVIETS NEVER RISKED MAJOR 
AGGRESSIVE ACTION AGAINST FREE EUROPE. 

SUT IT HAS ALSO BEEN A SOURCE OF CONCERN TO ALLIED COUNTRIES, WHERE 
MANY NON-COMMUNIST CRITICS OF THE UNITED STATES, AS WELL AS THE REDS 
THEMSELVES, EXPLOITED THE NOTION THAT A JUMPY AMERICA MIGHT SOME DAY 
PLUNGE THE WORLD INTO ATOMIC WAR, STRIKING BEFORE RUSSIA HAD THE BOMB. 

SUCH TALK NOW BECOMES ESSENTIALLY MEANINGLESS BECAUSE, AS 

ISENHOWER RECENTLY SAID, THE ONLY THING WORSE THAN WINNING 


WAR WOULD BE LOSING IT. SUCH COLD COMFORT AS IT 


A'S POSSESSION OF ATOMIC WEAPONS COULD MEAN AN END TO WORRY 
nett SOME AGGRESSIVE ACTION BY THIS COUNTRY. 

FROM A SOVIET POINT OF VIEW, ACCORDING TO THE STALEMATE THEORY, 
POSSESSION OF ATOMIC WEAPONS WOULD CREATE MOSTLY POWER TO ATTACK AND 
THE POWER TO RETALIATE AGAINST ATTACKe BUT IT WOULD NOT OFFER ANY 
REASONABLE ASSURANCE THAT IF THE REDS STARTED A FIGHT THEY WOULD NOT 
THEMSELVES SUFFER DESTRUCTION. IN OTHER WORDS, AMERICA'S POSSESSION OF 
ATOMIC WEAPONS MUST STILL BE CONSIDERED A POWERFUL CHECK ON ANY WAR- 

N THE KREMLIN.~ 
eee MATE THEORY APPARENTLY IS HAVING CONSIDERABLE INFLUENCE ON 
GOVERNMENT ESTIMATES THAT WAR IN THE NEAR FUTURE IS NOT LIKELY. THIS 
TS AN ALTERNATIVE TO THE NOTION THAT WHEN THE REDS HAD ATOMIC WEAPONS 
IN THEIR ARSENAL THE DANGER OF WAR WOULD IMMEDIATELY INCREASE. 

THERE IS NO EVIDENCE THAT RESPONSIBLE OFFICIALS THINK THE DANGER 
HAS ACTUALLY INCREASED. THE STALEMATE THEORY APPARENTLY LIES AT THE 
DOOT OF THEIR CONFIDENCE THAT FOR THE TIME BEING THE CHANCES AGAINST 
AN OPEN MILITARY OUT BREAK ARE GREATER THAN THE CHANCES FOR IT. 

’ THIS VIEW IS BOLSTERED BY THE LONG-HELD NOTION OF THE GOVERNMENT'S 
SOVIET EXPERTS THAT THE RUSSIANS PREFER TO PROMOTE THEIR DESIGNS BY 


ATIC MEANS IF AT ALL POSSIBLE.

WASHINGTON, OCTs 5 (AP)-VAL PETERSON, CIVIL DEFENSE ADMINISTRATOR, 
WARNED TONIGHT THAT AMERICA MAY BE FORCED TO MOVE ITS KEY FACTORIES 
UNDERGROUND OR “SEE ALL OF OUR PRODUCTION FACILITIES BLOWN UP SOME 
AFTERNOON" BY A SURPRISE RUSSIAN ATTACK. 

HIS AGENCY HAS COMPLETED A STUDY OUTLINING A VAST NETWORK OF UNDER- 
GROUND. SHELTERS FOR THE NATION'S CRITICAL TARGETS, PETERSON SAID oO 
ABC'S “REPORTER'S ROUNDUP.” THE COST OF SUCH A PROJECT, HE ADDED. was 
DIFFICULT TO ESTIMATE BUT WOULD RUN FROM 12 TO 90 BILLION DOLLARS? 

PETERSON SAID THE ONLY OTHER SOLUTION WAS DISPERSAL OF INDUSTRY 
AND EVACUATION OF CITIES. EVACUATION, HE ASSERTED, IS IMPRACTICAL 3E- 
CAUSE THERE IS NO CERTAINTY OF SUFFICIENT WARNING TIME OF AN ATTAce

BERLIN, OCT.7 (AP)-WILMELM PIECK, 77-YEAR-OLD COMMUNIST STREET 
; fo ROSE TO: THE ROLE OF ELDER STATESMAN, WAS REELECTED 
OF EAST GERMANY TODAY FOR A SECOND FOUR YEAR TERM. ——_— 

THE TWIN HOUSES OF PARLIAMENT IN THE SOVIET ZONE VOTED UNANIMOUSLY 
FOR PIECK AFTER IT WAS CLEAR THERE WERE NO OTHER CANDIDATES UNDER 
THE COMMUNIST SYSTEM. DEPUTY PRIME MINISTER OTTO NUSCHKE PROPOSED 
THAT PIECK BE CHOSEN BY ACCLAMATION BUT THE PARLIAMENT DECIDED To 
GO THROUGH THE MOTIONS OF CASTING BALLOTS. 

PIECk WIELDS LITTLE ACTUAL POWER AS PRESIDENT. WALTER ULBRICHT, 
BOSS OF THE SOCIALIST UNITY (COMMUNIST) PARTY AND PREMIER OTTO 
GROTEWOHL ARE THE MEN WHO RUN THE EAST GERMAN REPUBLIC UNDER THE 
WATCHFUL EYES OF THE SOVIETS. 

THE WHITE-HAIRED FORMER CABINET MAKER, EXTOLLED BY THE GERMAN 
REDS AS *THE WORKERS PRESIDENT,” WAITED OUTSIDE THE CHAMBER FOR THE 
VOTE THAT WAS PREARRANGED. : 

AS THE BALLOT WAS CAST, PIECK WAS USHERED INTO THE HALL WHERE 
HERMANN GOERING ONCE HELD BIG CONFERENCES ABOUT THE TROUBLES OF THE 


L 
T 
T 
K 


0 
WAZI AIR FORCE. THE RUBBER STAMP DEPUTIES SHOUTED AND CHEERED. 
THE ISSUE WAS SO LITTLE IN DOUBT THAT THE MARX-ENGELS SQUARE WAS 
ORGANIZED EARLIER FOR A BIG RALLY WITH A GIANT PICTURE OF PIECK AND 


\ RED-PAINTED SIGN HAILING HIM AS “OUR PRESIDENT” AND WISHING HIM 
LONG LIFEe | 

JOHANNES DIECKMANN, PRESIDENT OF PARLIAMENT, SAID THE 
UNANIMOUS ELECTION OF PIECK IS IN CONTRAST WITH THE ELECTION oF 
PRESIDENT EISENHOWER "WHO WAS PUT INTO OFFICE ONLY FTER MONTHS OF 
BITTER WRANGLING AND WITH A NOT TOO CONVINCING MAJORITY." 

THE COMBINED VOLKSKAMMER AND LAENDERKAMMER, IN CASTING A COMPLETE 
VOTE FOR PIECK, KEPT INTACT THEIR RECORD OF NEVER HAVING OPPOSED IN 
ANY WAY A COMMUNIST GOVERNMENT PROPOSAL. 

THE SESSION WAS CALLED TO OBSERVE THE FOURTH ANNIVERSARY OF THE 
FOUNDING OF THE "GERMAN DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC.® LAST NIGHT SOVIET 
PREMIER GEORGI MALENKOV SENT HIS BEST WISHES. THE ANNIVERSARY WAS 
DECLARED A STATE HOLIDAY. THROUGHOUT THE RUSSIAN ZONE THE COMMUNIST 
LEADERS ORGANIZED CELEBRATIONS.

UNITED NATIONS, NeYs, OCT.S (AP)-IN A SURPRISE VOTE TODAY, THE UNITED

FOR QUICK WORLD RATIFICATION OF A U.N. PACT TO OUTLAW GENOCIDE, OR 
MASS RACE OR RELIGIOUS EXTERMINATION. 

NEITHER COUNTRY HAS RATIFIED THE CONVENTION. SECRETARY OF STATE 
DULLES ANNOUNCED EARLY LAST SUMMER THAT THE UNITED STATES THEN WOULD

OFESSOR OF INTERNATIONAL LAW WHO FRAMED THE GENOCIDE CONVENTION Now 
PATIFLED BY 42 COUNTRIES, PREDICTED THAT THE UNITED STATES AND RUSSIA

THEIR FAMILIES AWAY "ON VACATION. |

ZONE A, WAS DESTROYED BY YUGOSLAVS.

EACH COUNTRY HAS A NUMBER OF OTHER REASONS, SOME VALID. SOME NOT. 
ITALY, ON THE ONE HAND, CLAIMS THE TERRITORY {1S RIGHTFULLY A PART 
OF THE ITALIAN NATION. YUGOSLAVIA CONTENDS IT SHOULD HAVE THE AREA 
AS PAYMENT FOR LOSSES SUFFERED AT ITALIAN HANDS IN WORLD WAR II. 

THE TERRITORY, ON THE GULF OF TRIESTE AT THE HEAD OF THE 
ADRIATIC, COMPRISES A TOTAL OF 320 SQUARE MILES AND HAS A POPULATION 
OF ABOUT 350,000. IT CONTAINS THE BIG PORT CITY OF TRIESTE, WHICH FOR 
CENTURIES SERVED THE LAND-LOCKED STATES OF CENTRAL EUROPE. 

THROUGH ITS VARIED, 1,000-YEAR HISTORY THE PORT AND SURROUNDING 
AREA WAS TWICE BEFORE A FREE TERRITORY, AT OTHER TIMES WAS UNDER 
AUSTRIAN OR ITALIAN 

TRIESTE WAS PART OF AUSTRIA FROM THE 14TH TO THE 18TH CENTURIES, 
THEN WAS MADE A FREE TERRITORY FOR NEARLY A HUNDRED YEARS. FOR 
BRIEF PERIODS IT WAS TWICE PART OF THE BONAPARTE KINGDOM OF ITALY, 

BUT IN 1813 WAS RETURNED TO AUSTRIA. 

ITALY TOOK OVER THE WHOLE ISTRIAN PENINSULA, INCLUDING THE 
TRIESTE TERRITORY, AFTER AUSTRIA'S DEFEAT IN WORLD WAR I.  YUGO- 
SLAVIA WAS ESTABLISHED AS AN INDEPENDENT NATION AT THE SAME TIME. 

BY THE END OF WORLD WAR II, YUGOSLAVIA SOLDIERS HAD OCCUPIED MUCH 
OF THE ISTRIAN PENINSULA AND WANTED THE PORT OF TRIESTE AS WELL. 

HOWEVER, IN 1947 UNDER TERMS OF THE ITALIAN PEACE TREATY, THE BIG 
FOUR FOREIGN MINISTERS COUNCIL SET UP THE AREA AS A FREE TERRITORY. 
FOR ADMINISTRATION, IT WAS DIVIDED INTO TWO ZONES. ZONE A, COM- 
PRISING ABOUT ONE-THIRD OF THE TOTAL AREA, A LARGE PART OF THE 
POPULATION AND THE PORT. WAS PLACED UNDER BRITISH-AMERICAN CONTROL. 
ZONE B, SOUTH OF THE PORT ALONG THE ADRIATIC, WAS PLACED UNDER 
YUGOSLAV JURISDICTION.

IN 1948 THE BRITISH, AMERICANS AND FRENCH BOOSTED 4 ITALIAN

THE DISPUTE EXPLODED INTO AN ALL-OUT WORD WAR LAST AUGUST, 

SHORTLY AFTER ITALY GOT A NEW PREMIER, GIUSEPPE PELLA. 

HE SET OFF THE EXPLOSION BY INTERPRETING A YUGOSLAV PRESS |

MOVEMENTS. 


AFTER A WESTERN DIPLOMATIC FLURRY, BOTH COUNTRIES OFFERED THEIR 
OWN SOLUTIONS. 

PELLA PROPOSED A PLEBISCITE IN BOTH ZONES TO DETERMINE THE WISHES 
OF THE PEOPLE, WITH ALL TROOPS TO CLEAR OUT BEFORE THE VOTING. 

TITO DEMANDED THAT THE PORT ITSELF BE INTERNATIONALIZED AND THE 
REST OF THE TERRITORY BE TURNED OVER TO YUGOSLAVIA. SINCE HE WOULD 
NOT PULL YUGOSLAV TROOPS OUT OF ZONE B, THE PLEBISCITE HAD NO CHANCE 
OF SUCCESS. 

IN ANY EVENT, BOTH COUNTRIES REJECTED THE OTHER'S PROPOSALS. 

THURSDAY, BRITAIN AND THE UNITED STATES ANNOUNCED THEY WOULD 
WITHDRAW THEIR 7,000 TROOPS FROM ZONE A; LEAVING IT UNDER ITALIAN 
CONTROL. THEY HOPED THE DECISION WOULD EVENTUALLY BRING AN END TO 
THE ITALIAN-YUGOSLAV FEUD BY PUTTING BOTH SIDES ON EQUAL TERMS.

CAMP FRIEDLAND. GERMANY, OCT. 10 (AP)-THE RUSSIANS TODAY WERE 
REPORTED HOLDING 200 GERMAN SCIENTISTS WHO RETUSED TO RENEW CONTRACTS 
TO WORK ON ATOMIC RESEARCH PROJECTS BEHIND THE IRON CURTAIN. 

THE REPORT WAS MADE BY GERMAN PRISONERS OF WAR WHO HAVE JUST 
RETURNED AFTER SPENDING 10 YEARS IN RUSSIAN CAPTIVITY. 

THE RETURNEES, WHO WOULD NOT PERMIT USE OF THEIR NAMES FOR 
PERSONAL REASONS, SAID THEY MET THE GERMAN SCIENTISTS AT CAMP 
DERNITZA, FIVE MILES FROM KIEV, IN THE SOVIET UKRAINE. 

THE REPATRIATED SOLDIERS SAID THAT THE SCIENTISTS, INCLUDING 
PHYSICISTS, CHEMISTS AND HIGHLY SPECIALIZED TECHNICIANS, WERE RECRUITED 
IN 1947 TO SIGN TWO-YEAR CONTRACTS TO WORK FOR THE RUSSIANS AT A 
SECRET ATOMIC RESEARCH INSTITUTE AT SUCHUMI, ON THE BLACK SEA. 

WHEN THE SCIENTISTS REFUSED TO RENEW THE CONTRACTS IN 1949, THEY 
SAID, THEY WERE TRANSFERRED TO CAMP DETNITZA TO AWAIT A PROMISED RETURN 


TO GERMANY. 
hpeiee’ THE POWS SAID, THE SCIENTISTS ARE STILL THERE. THEIR REPORT 
WHILE LIVING ON THE BLACK SEA, THE GERMAN ATOM EXPERTS WERE HIGHLY 
PAID AND GIVEN EXCELLENT LIVING tonDITIONS, INCLUDING GOOD HOMES, 
PRIVATE BEACHES AND A CAR AND CHAUFFER. 
WHEN THEY REFUSED TO SIGN UP AGAIN, THEY WERE IMMEDIATELY SHIPPED 


OFF TO CAMP DERNITZA AND REGARDED AS PRISONERS. EXCEPT FOR 30 TOP 
SCIENTISTS ALL OF THEM WERE PUT TO HARD LABOR.

WASHINGTON, OCT. 11 (AP)-SEN. KEFAUVER (D-TENN) SAID TODAY THE 
PEOPLE ARE ENTITLED TO KNOW IF THE JOINT CHIEFS OF STAFF BELIEVE 
AMERICA'S LARGER CITIES CAN'T BE DEFENDED AGAINST ATOMIC ATTACK. 

KEFAUVER, A MEMBER OF THE SENATE ARMED SERVICES COMMITTEE, SAID IN 
AN INTERVIEW THAT IF ATOMIC RETALIATION AGAINST AN AGGRESSOR IS RE- 
GARDED BY THE NATION'S MILITARY CHIEFS AS THE BEST DEFENSE, THE 
PUBLIC SHOULD KNOW THAT. 

I DON'T GO ALONG WITH THE PHILOSOPHY THAT WE CAN AFFORD TO 
SACRIFICE MASSES OF POPULATION IN OUR BIG CITIES IN CASE OF AN 
ATTACK," HE SAID. "I THINK SOMETHING CAN BE DONE TO DEFEND THOSE 
CITIES AND WHAT CAN BE DONE OUGHT TO BE DONE, WHETHER THE BUDGET IS 
BALANCED OR NOT.”

UNETED TIONS NeYe, OCTs11 (AP)-NORTH KOREA JOINED RED CHINA 
IN A CABLE MADE PUBLIC HERE TODAY DEMANDING NEW TALKS AT PANMUNJOM 
ON THE MAKEUP, TIME AND DATE OF A KOREAN PEACE CONFERENCE. THE 
COMMUNISTS ARE STILL INSISTING THAT RUSSIA, INDIA, INDONESIA, BURMA AND 
PAKISTAN BE ADMITTED TO THE CONFERENCE AS 
NEUTRALS. 

RED CHINA'S DEMAND ARRIVED YESTERDAY BY WAY OF SWEDEN AFTER THE 
PEIPING REGIME'’S PREMIER AND FOREIGN MINISTER CHOU-EN LAI VOICED IT 
ON A RADIO BROADCAST. 

THE NORTH KOREAN CABLE, SIGNED BY FOREIGN MINISTER NAM-IL, ONE OF THI 
KOREAN ARMISTICE NEGOTIATORS, CAME BY WAY OF MOSCOW. IT NOTED THAT 
A SIMILAR CABLE WAS SENT DIRECTLY TO THE U.sS~s STATE DEPARTMENT IN 
REPLY TO THE THREE U.S NOTES DEMANDING A QUICK MEETING TO ARRANGE 
THE 

UeN« OFFICIALS HERE LOOKED TO A HIGH-LEVEL WASHINGTON MEETING 
OF THE 16 UsN. ALLIES TOMORROW TO DECIDE WHETHER THE NEW COMMUNIST 
DEMANDS WOULD BE MET. NEITHER OFFICIALS NOR DELEGATES HERE 
FORESAW ANY HASTY ACTION TO BRING THE KOREAN 
QUESTION BACK FROM THE BOTTOM OF THE ASSEMBLY POLITICAL COMMITTEE'S 
PILE. 

THE UNITED STATES WAS DESIGNATED SPOKESMAN FOR THE 16 BY THE U.N. 
GENERAL ASSEMBLY IN AUGUST, WHICH/AD THE SAME TIME RULED OUT NEUTRALS 
AT THE PEACE CONFERENCE. SINCE THE OPENING OF THE EIGHTH ASSEMBLY, 
HOWEVER, U.S» CHIEF DELEGATE HENRY CABOT LODGE JR. HAS TWICE TOLD 
DELEGATES IN COMMITTEE MEETINGS THAT THE DEMAND OF THE _ 

COMMUNISTS TO SEAT NEUTRALS AT THE CONFERENCE COULD BE TAKEN UP BY THE 
CONFERENCE ITSELF. 

RUSSIA'S ANDREI VISHINSKY IN A POLITICAL COMMITTEE DEBATE ASKED 
LODGE DIRECTLY WHETHER HE MEANT THAT THE UNITED STATES WOULD 
AGREE TO THE DEMAND. LODGE SHOOK HIS HEAD BUT NEVER STATED 
THE UeSe FINAL STAND IN WORDS. Mo *’ 

THE UNITED STATES HAS BEEN PRESSING FOR THE CONFERENCE TO BEGIN 
BY OCT.15--FOUR DAYS FROM NOW--IN GENEVA, SAN FRANCISCO OR HONOLULU. 

UNDER THE TERMS OF THE KOREAN ARMISTICE AGREEMENT, THE 
CONFERENCE DEADLINE WOULD BE OCT.28. DELEGATES HERE AGREE, HOWEVER, 
THAT THE ACTUAL DATE IS UNIMPORTANT. 

THE NEW COMMUNIST DEMANDS STILL LIMIT THE PROPOSED PANMUNJOM 
TALKS TO PRELIMINARIES AND THERE WAS CURIOSITY WHETHER THE UNITED 
STATES WAS READY TO AGREE TO SUCH TALKS WITH THE IMPLIED PRE- 
CONDITION THAT THE QUESTION OF THE NEUTRALS SHOULD BE TAKEN UP. 

ON THE OTHER HAND, THE NEW COMMUNIST NOTE DID NOT SAY THE 
PANMUNJOM CONFERENCE "MUST" SETTLE QUESTIONS OF TIME, PLACE AND 
MAKEUP But ONLY THAT IT "SHOULD".

CANBERRA. AUSTRALIA, OCTe 13 CAP)-AUSTRALIA HAS 
PACT WITH BRITAIN FOR THE SALE OF URANIUM ORE AS A RESULT OF THE VI 
OF BRITISH PAYMASTER GENERAL LORD CHERWELL, AUSTRALIAN PRIME MINIST 
ReGeMENZIES TOLD THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES TODAY. 

"WE WOULD NOT DREAM OF ENTERING ANY AGREEMENT WHICH DEPRIVED 
OUR_OWN COUNTRY OF OUR FUTURE REQUIREMENTS OF THIS VALUABLE 
MATERIAL.” HE SAID. 

"OUR TASK IS CLEAR FROM FIRST TO LAST, THAT SUBJECT TO DEFENSE 
REQUIREMENTS WE DON'T DEPRIVE OUR COUNTRY OF MATERIAL WHICH MAY TURN 
OUT TO BE OF IMMENSE SIGNIFICANCE TO AUSTRALIAN DEVELOPMENTe NOBODY 
HAS CONTEMPLATED SUCH A THING." 

AUSTRALIA SELLS URANIUM ORE NOW UNDER CONTRACTS WITH THE 
COMBINED DEVELOPMENT AGENCY, WHICH ACTS ON BEHALF OF BOTH OF THE UNITED 
STATES AND UNITED KINGDOM. 

MENZIES REFUSED TO GIVE ANY INFORMATION ON THE PRICE PAID. SAYING 
SUCH DISCLOSURES WOULD ENABLE COMMUNIST COUNTRIES TO CALCULATE 
AUSTRALIAN URANIUM PRODUCTION.

OWN.

ROME, OCT. 15 (AP)-PREMIER GIUSEPPE PELLA TONIGHT GAVE THE U.S*, 
BRITAIN AND FRANCE ITALY'S PROPOSALS ON THE TRIESTE SITUATION FoR 
CONSIDERATION AT THE BIG THREE FOREIGN MINISTERS MEETING IN LONDON. 

HE CALLED IN U.sSe AMBASSADOR CLARE BOOTHE LUCE, BRITISH 
AMBASSADOR SIR VICTOR MALLET AND FRENCH AMBASSADOR JACQUES FOUQUES 

THE UsSe AND BRITAIN LAST WEEK ANNOUNCED THEY WERE EVACUATING 
THEIR OCCUPATION TROOPS FROM ZONE A OF THE TRIESTE FREE TERRITORY AND 
TURNING IT OVER TO ITALY. YUGOSLAVIA, WHICH OCCUPIES ZONE B, SAID IF 
ITALIAN TROOPS SET FOOT IN ZONE A THE YUGOSLAV ARMY WOULD TAKE ACTION. 

PELLA WAS BELIEVED TO HAVE MADE CLEAR TO THE BIG THREE REPRESENTAT— 
IVES THAT ITALY WANTS TO SETTLE THE ITALO-YUGOSLAV DIFFICULTIES WITHOUT 
FORCE AND IS PREPARED TO GIVE YUGOSLAVIA ASSURANCES TO THIS EFFECT. 

PELLA, WAS SAID TO HAVE PRESENTED THE VIEW THAT ITALY IS 
PREPARED TO PARTICIPATE IN A CONFERENCE WITH YUGOSLAVIA OVER THE 
ULTIMATE DISPOSITION OF THE STRATEGIC ADRIATIC TERRITORY AS SOON 
AS THEY ARE ON "EVEN TERMS." THIS COULD MEAN EITHER? 

1. IF ITALIAN TROOPS OCCUPY ZONE A AS YUGOSLAVIA OCCUPIES ZONE Bz 

2. IF YUGOSLAVIA WITHDRAWS FROM ZONE B AND ITALY DOES NOT 
OCCUPY ZONE A. 

AN INFORMANT SAID PELLA "VERY PROBABLY" MADE CLEAR THAT EVEN IF 
ITALIAN TROOPS DID ENTER ZONE A, AS THE ALLIES EXPECT WHEN THEIR FORCES 
WITHDRAW, THIS IN NO WAY WOULD CONSTITUTE A BRFAK OF 
THE PEACE OR INDICATE ANY ITALIAN DESIRE TO USE FORCE.

ISTANBUL, TURKEY, OCT. 15 (AP)-THREE ARMY OFFICERS TODAY BEGAN THE 
MASS TRIAL OF 167 MEN AND WOMEN CHARGED WITH A COMMUNIST 


PLOT TO OVERTHROW TURKEY'S GOVERNMENT. 

MANY OF THE DEFENDANTS HAVE BEEN HELD IN JAIL FOR LONG PERIODS, SOME 
FOR AS MUCH AS TWO YEARS, WHILE THE SECRET POLICE COMPLETED 
THEIR INVESTIGATIONS. 

ALL BUT THREE OF THE DEFENDANTS WERE PRESENT AS THE TRIAL OPENED 
BEFORE THE THREE-MAN TRIBUNAL. THE MISSING TRIO WERE REPORTED 
ILL IN A HOSPITAL. | 

THE TRIAL PROVIDED THE FIRST NEWS OF MANY OF THE 
DEFENDANTS FOR THEIR RELATIVES AND FRIENDS SINCE THEIR ARREST. THEY 
HAD DROPPED FROM SIGHT COMPLETELY AFTER BEING PICKED UP.

RESENTED THEIR WIDESPREAD ADOPTION.

RESULTING LOW STANDARD OF LIVING FOR THE RUSSIAN PEOPLE.

FLEW TO MOSCOW WITH Us Se AMBASSADOR CHARLES E. BOHLEN. HE ALSO 
VISITED ENGLAND, SWEDEN, FINLAND, DENMARK, SPAIN, SWITZERLAND AND 
FRANCE DURING A’MONTH'S TRIP.

WASHINGTON, 15 (AP)-SENeMALONE SAID TODAY THAT 77 
PER CENT OF THE VALUE OF ALL GOVERNMENT STOCKPILE MATERIALS NOW IN THIS 
COUNTRY WERE PURCHASED ABROAD. 

MALONE, CHAIRMAN OF A SENATE INTERIOR wire git MADE THE 
STATEMENT AFTER A DAY-LONG HEARING BEHIND CLOSED DOOR DURING WHICH HE 
DISCUSSED STOCKPILING PROBLEMS WITH SEVERAL GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS. 

MALQNE TOLD NEWSMEN AFTER THE SESSION THAT HE SEES A "TERRIBLE 
DANGER" IN WHAT HE CALLED THE RELIANCE ON FOREIGN SOURCES OF SUPPLY. 

HE SAID THIS HAS DEVELOPED DURING THE PAST 20 YEARS» 

HE CITED A WEST POINT TEXTBOOK, CALLED "WAR MATERIALS IN WAR AND 
PEACE", AS EVIDENCE THAT THE GOVERNMENT HAS COMMITTED ITSELF TO THE 
PURCHASE OF SCARCE AND STRATEGIC MATERIALS ON THE BASIS OF COST ALONE, 
WITH LITTLE OR NO CONSIDERATION FOR ENCOURAGING HIGHER COST DOMESTIC 
PRODUCTION AND MANUFACTURE. THIS POLICY, HE SAID, REFUSES TO TAKE INTO 
ACCOUNT THAT WAGES PAID ABROAD AND OTHER PRODUCTION COSTS ARE USUALLY 
MUCH LOWER THAN HERE. 

MALONE ALSO SAID THE GOVERNMENT HAS DELIBERATELY BOUGHT TUNGSTEN 
ABROAD, BROUGHT IT TO THIS COUNTRY DUTY-FREE. AND THEN SOLD IT TO 


PRIVATE Sag 2 FOR USE IN WAR PRODUCTION. HE CALLED 


THIS A “DELIBERATE EVASION” OF UsSe TARIFFS.

COMPANIES CANNOT JUSTIFY A GREATER WORK FORCE,

"\ SURVEY OF OUR DEFENSE ACTIVITIES AND THOSE OF OUR ALLIES 
LEADS ME TO THE CONCLUSION THAT, EVEN TAKING INTO ACCOUNT THE NEEDS 
OF A REALISTIC CONTINENTAL DEFENSE PROGRAM FOR THE PROTECTION OF THE 
ONL TED STATES BETTER PLANNING, MORE REALISTIC BALANCING OF THE ELE- 
MENTS OF MILITARY STRENGTH, AND THE ELIMINATION OF DUPLICATION WITHIN 
COUNTRIES, INCLUDING OUR OWN, AND BETWEEN ALLIED COUNTRIES, WILL RESULT 
IN SUFFICLENT SAVINGS TO PERMIT THE DEVELOPMENT OF A REASONABLE MILI- 
TARY POSTURE IN THE WESTERN WORLD WITHIN THE ECONOMIC CAPABILITIES 
AVAILABLE TO US 

"AS AN ESSENTIAL PART OF THIS POSITIVE APPROACH, WE MUST REASSESS 
OUR STRATEGIC PLANNING AND LOGISTICS IN THE LIGHT OF TECHNOLOGICAL 
ADVANCES, AND HAVE THE COURAGE TO DISCARD THE OUTMODED PROCEDURES AND 
WEAPONS WHICH WILL NO LONGER SERVE MORE THAN TRADITION. 

"WE NO LONGER CAN AFFORD TO PREPARE FOR EVERY CONCEIVABLE KIND 
OF WARe WE NO LONGER CAN AFFORD THE LUXURY OF THE "STATUS QUO’ 
IN STRATEGIC PLANNING. THE DAY HAS PASSED WHEN WE CAN ACCEPT LESS 
THAN THE MOST EFFECTIVE AND EFFICIENT LOGISTIC SUPPLY AND ORGANIZATION. 
SUCH AN APPROACH WILL REQUIRE MANY COURAGEOUS DECISIONS, BUT 
IT APPEARS TO ME TO CONTAIN ALL THE ELEMENTS OF WISDOM.

BETWEEN THE TWO COUNTRIES.

INCLUDING FRENCH FORCES. IN ADDITION, COMMAND OF FOUR ROYAL

OF THE FRENCH WILL REVERT TO CONTROL OF THE KING.

AS FRENCH UNION TROOPS BUT MADE UP OF CAMBODIAN SOLDIERS.

BERN, SWITZERLAND, OCT. 19 (AP)-THE SWISS GOVERNMENT TODAY ORDERED 
COL. ARMIN DAENIKER, HEAD OF THE SWISS PRISONER-OF-WAR COMMISSION IN 
KOREA. TO TRY TO AVOID THE USE OF FORCE AGAINST PRISONERS "UNDER 
ALL CIRCUMSTANCES." 

DReALFRED ZEHNDER, HEAD OF THE POLITICAL DIVISION OF THE SWISS 
FOREIGN OFFICE, TOLD’A NEWS CONFERENCE THE INTERROGATION AND 
"EXPLANATORY INTERVIEWS" OF CHINESE AND NORTH KOREAN PRISONERS HAD 
BEGUN WITHOUT INCIDENT, BUT. NOW REQUIRED THE USE OF FORCE. 

"THE FEDERAL COUNCIL (CABINET) HAS NOW GIVEN THE SWISS DELEGATION 
CATEGORIC INSTRUCTIONS THAT SWITZERLAND SEEKS TO AVOID THE USE OF 
FORCE UNDER ALL CIRCUMSTANCES,” DRe«SEHNDER DECLARED. "SWITZERLAND 
COULD NEVER BE A PARTY TO A USE OF FORCE AGAINST PRISONERS-OF- 

WAR. THAT WOULD BE A VIOLATION NOT ONLY OF THE GENEVA CON- 
VENTIONS. BUT OF THE INTERNATIONAL LAW IN GENERAL." 

DR. ZEHNDER DISCLOSED THAT DIVISIONAL COL. (MAJeGEN.) FRITZ 
RIHNER. HEAD OF THE SWISS DETACHMENT ON THE ARMISTICE SUPERVISORY 
COMMISSION. WOULD BE REPLACED AT THE END OF THE YEAR BY DIVISIONAL 
COL. PAUL WACKER. RIHNER IS RETURNING HOME AS SCHEDULED AT THE END 
OF HIS SIX-MONTHS CONTRACT, DR«ZEXNDER DECLARED, THOUGH THE CONTRACTS 
OF MOST OTHER MEMBERS OF THE SWISS DETACHMENT ARE BEING RENEWED. 
COL«RIHNER HAS BEEN CRITICIZED IN THE SWISS PRESS FOR HIS INABILITY 
TO SPEAK ENGLISH, BUT THIS INABILITY "DID NOT INTERFERE WITH THE 
SATISFACTORY PERFORMANCE OF HIS MISSION," DR«ZEHNDER SAID.

BY LYNN HEINZERLING 

BELGRADE, YUGOSLAVIA, OCT. 19 (AP)-BORBA 
LEADERS OF YUGOSLAVIA, WARNED TONIGHT THAT {TALIAN OCCUPATION OF 
TRIESTE'S ZONE A "WITH OR WITHOUT TROOPS IS THE SAME THING" AND IS 
UNACCEPTABLE TO YUGOSLAVIA. | 

THE DECLARATION “WITH OR WITHOUT TROOPS" WAS SIGNIFICANT IN THAT 
THERE HAS BEEN MUCH SPECULATION AS TO WHAT THE YUGOSLAV ATTITUDE 
WOULD BE TOWARD CONTROL OF ZONE A BY ITALIAN POLICE INSTEAD OF TROOPS. 
THE OFFICIAL NEWSPAPER PUT POLICE AND TROOPS IN THE SAME CATEGORY. 

FOR THE SECOND DAY BELGRADE REMAINED IN PUZZLED ANXIETY AS THE 
GOVERNMENT CLAMPED A RIGID BAN ON ANY OFFICIAL REACTION TO THE WESTERN 
FOREIGN MINISTERS" PROPOSAL FOR A FIVE-POWER CONFERENCE ON TRIESTE. 

BELGRADE NEWSPAPER COMMENTATORS PARTICULARLY WERE EXERCISED BY 
UNOFFICIAL INTERPRETATIONS FROM LONDON THAT THE CONFERENCE WOULD 
OPEN ON THE PREMISE THAT ZONE A WOULD BE TURNED OVER TO ITALY IN ANY 


CASE. 
"YUGOSLAVIA WILL NOT PERMIT ITALY TO TAKE ZONE A," BORBA SAID. 
THESE 


“THAT IS THE ESSENTIAL FACT_IN THIS CASE AND THAT IS 
BELGRADE REMAINED QUIET AND UNDISTURBED IN CONTRAST TO THE WILD 
DEMONSTRATION OF OCT. 3 WHEN THE BRITISH-AMERICAN DECISION ON TRIESTE 
WAS ANNOUNCED. THE TWO NATIONS ANNOUNCED THEY WOULD WITHDRAW 
OCCUPATION TROOPS FROM ZONE A AND HAND THE ADMINISTRATION OF THE 
ZONE OVER TO ITALY. 
CALLED TO FULFILL 


BORBA SAID THAT IF THE FIVE-POWER CONFERENCE WERE 
THE BRITISH-AMERICAN DECISION IT COULD ONLY RESULT IN “A FURTHER 


SHARPENING OF THE SITUATION." 

"IT IS EVIDENT," THE NEWSPAPER ADDED, “THE IDEA OF A CONFERENCE 
WHICH WOULD TAKE AS ITS STARTING POINT THE OCT. 8 DECISION WOULD BE 
SENSELESS BECAUSE IT WOULD MEAN THE FULFILLMENT OF ITALIAN AGGRESSION 
WHICH IS WHAT WE CATEGORICALLY HAVE OPPOSED AND WILL FIRMLY FIGHT. 

TIME ALL BELGRADE NEWSPAPERS, URGED AN IMMEDIATE 


THE VOICE OF COMMUNIST 


AT THE SAME . 
CONFERENCE OF THE UNITED STATES, BRITAIN, YUGOSLAVIA AND ITALY *TO 
REMOVE THE PRESENT DANGEROUS sit ATIONe” THE OTHER COUNTRY IN THE 


PROPOSED FIVE-POWER CONFERENCE IS FRANCE. 

VICE PRESIDENT ALEXANDER RANKOVIC SPEAKING IN THE MOUNTAIN TOWN OF 

PEC NEAR THE ALBANIAN BORDER, SAID3 “WE WILL NEVER PERMIT ITALIANS TO

WASHINGTON, OCT. 19 CAP)-THE ARMY SAID TODAY AWOL (ABSENT WITHOUT 
LEAVE) AND DESERTION RATES HAVE DROPPED MORE THAN 30 PER CENT SINCE 
COMMANDERS WERE AUTHORIZED TO SHIP CONVICTED RUNAWAYS TO KOREA. 

ABOUT 6,900 AWOLS HAVE BEEN SENT TO THE FAR EAST SINCE THE ARMY 
ADOPTED THIS POLICY EARLY THIS YEAR, A SPOKESMAN ARMY SAID. 

THE ARMY DECLINES TO GIVE EXACT FIGURES ON UNAUTHORIZED ABSENCES 
AND DESERTIONS. BUT LAST JANUARY OFFICERS DISCLOSED THAT ABOUT 6,000 
MEN EACH MONTH WERE FAILING TO BE WHERE THEY WERE SUPPOSED TO BE, 
USUALLY JUST PRIOR TO EMBARKATION FOR DUTY IN THE KOREAN BATTLE 

AT THAT TIME THE ARMY ALSO REPORTED ABOUT 11,000 DESERTERS WERE AT 
LARGE. CURRENT REGULATIONS MAKE A MAN LIABLE FOR COURT MARTIAL AS 
A DESERTER IF AN UNAUTHORIZED ABSENCE EXTENDS FOR MORE THAN 
30 DAYS. AWOLS ARE THOSE WHO ARE ABSENT LESS THAN 30 DAYS.

000,000 ALLOCATED FOR REHABILITATION," BROWNSON SAID. "BUT IF ALL 
THE AGENCY EMPLOYES STAY THERE LONG. ENOUGH, A SIZEABLE PORTION OF THE 
TOTAL FUND CAN BE USED WITHOUT ANY RECONSTRUCTION TO SHOW FOR IT." 
BROWNSON SAID RHEE'S PLANS FOR REHABILITATION CALL FOR CONSTRUCTION 
OF THE LARGEST RADIO TRANSMITTER IN THE WORLD, A SUPER HIGHWAY BETWEEN 
SEOUL AND PUSAN, A CHAIN OF MODERN TOURIST HOTELS FOR AMERICAN SOLDIERS 
AND THEIR FAMIL{ES AND THE RAZING OF THE BURNED OUT CAPITOL BUILDING 
AND ERECTION OF A NEW ONE.

HA OCT. 21 (AP)-ONE OF THE BIGGEST FRENCH OFFENSIVES 
OF THE ENDOCHINA WAR APPEARED HEADED TONIGHT FOR AN EARLY WINDUP UNLESS

AL THE HIGH COMMAND MAINTAINED SILENCE, THERE SEEMED LITTLE

PHU NHO QUAN OR THANH HOA, STRONGHOLDS OF VIETMINH DIVISIONS 320 AND 
304 RESPECTIVELY SOUTH OF THE FRENCH-HELD RED RIVER DELTA. 

FRENCH AND VIETNAMESE TROOPS ARE IN A STRONG POSITION ON THE 
STRATEGIC HIGHWAY CALLED THE MANDARIN ROAD WITHIN 20 MILES OF THANH 
HOA, BUT HAVE MADE NO FURTHER ADVANCE TOWARD THAT CITY IN THE LAST 
4S HOURS. TROOPS LEFT BEHIND TO COUNTER ANY VIETMINH ATTACK 
FROM THE REAR HAVE CONCENTRATED ON MOPPING UP SMALL UNITS OF THE COM- 
MUNIST-LED REBELS SOUTH AND SOUTHWEST OF PHU NHO QUAN AND SEEKING WAR 
SUPPLIES TO DESTROY. 

THE LAND, SEA AND AIR DRIVE STARTED OCT. 15. THE FRENCH 
COMMANDER IN CHIEF, GEN. HENRI NAVARRE, THREW MANY THOUSANDS OF MEN 
INTO THE OFFENSIVE:

CAPTURE OF LESS THAN 50 AND CUTTING OF HIGHWAYS SOUTH OF THANH HOA 
OVER WHICH THE REBELS MIGHT HAVE GOTTEN REINFORCEMENTS FROM CENTRAL 

‘THE FRENCH, IN STARTING THE DRIVE, SAID THEIR PRIME TARGET WAS 
DESTRUCTION OF REBEL WAR DEPOTS, THUS PARALYZING ANY PLANS OF THE Two 
VIETMINH DIVISIONS FOR ASSAULTING THE RED RIVER DELTA. 

RENE COGNY, FRENCH COMMANDER IN NORTH INDOCHINA, 

*I SEEK BATTLE WITH THE TWO REBEL DIVISIONS. I HOLD NO INTEREST

LANTIC TREATY ORGANIZATION (NATO) AND OTHER FRIENDLY NATIONS.

WASHINGTON, OCT. 22 (AP)-PLANS ARE ABOUT COMPLETE FOR FUNNELING U.S. 
MILITARY AID TO WESTERN EUROPEAN COUNTRIES THROUGH THE PROJECTED EURO- 
PEAN DEFENSE COMMUNITY (EDC) AS SOON AS IT IS RATIFIED.

TARY OF STATE DULLES AND OTHER TOP OFFICIALS AS CONFIDENT THAT THE LONG- 
STALLED EDC TREATY WILL BE FINALLY APPROVED IN THE NEXT THREE OR FOUR 
THAT ACTION WOULD CLEAR THE WAY FOR REARMING OF WEST GERMANY, THE 
ONLY NATION WHICH HAS RATIFIED IT SO FAR. OTHER SIGNERS ARE FRANCE, 
ITALY, BELGIUM, THE NETHERLANDS AND LUXEMBOURG, 
STATE DEPARTMENT INFORMANTS SAID A SPECIAL AGREEMENT COVERING THE 
DELIVERY OF AMERICAN AID TO EDC, BEING WORKED OUT WITH A DEFENSE COM- 
MUNITY PREPARATORY COMMISSION AT PARIS, IS SUBSTANTIALLY COMPLETED. 
IN GENERAL IT FOLLOWS THE LINE OF AGREEMENTS REQUIRED BY CONGRESS 
WITH ALL THE INDIVIDUAL COUNTRIES RECEIVING U. S. ASSISTANCE.

APPROVAL. TECHNICAL PROVISIONS COVER PRESENCE OF AMERICAN PERSONNEL 
IN THE AREAS WHERE WEAPONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE RELEASED AND USED.

BY ALLAN JACKS (350) 
REGGIO CALABRIA, ITALY, OCT. 23 (AP)-RESCUE WORKERS SEARCHED TODAY 
THROUGH WRECKED HOMES IN A’ DOZEN SMALL VILLAGES OF THIS SOUTHERN ITALINA 
PROVINCE FOR VICTIMS OF DEVASTATING FLASH FLOODS THAT MAY HAVE CLAIMED 
AS MANY AS 100 LIVES. s 
TORRENTIAL RAINS CONTINUED TO POUR ON THE STRICKEN AREA FROM REGGIO 
CALABRIA ALONG THE IONIAN SEA THIS MORNING. THEY STOPPED ABRUPTOY 
AT NOON, BUT HEAVY GRAY CLOUDS STILL HUNG OVER THE AREA, THREATENING 

IN THE REGGIO CALABRIA AREA ALONE 53 DEAD HAVE BEEN ACCOUNTED For. 
SCORES ARE MISSING. | 

HUNDREDS WERE INJURED IN THE DISASTER, THE WORST HERE SINCE AN 
EARTHQUAKE LEVELLED THE REGION IN 1903. RESIDENTS SAID THE 
DAMAGE, ESTIMATED IN THE BILLIONS OF LIRE, WAS FAR GREATER THAN THAT 
CAUSED BY SIMILAR INNUNDATIONS TwO YEARS AGO. 

THE FLOODS STRUCK WITHOUT WARNING JUST BEFORE DAWN YESTERDAY, CATCHING 
MANY PERSONS ASLEEP IN THEIR BEDS. THEY WERE PRECEDED BY 12 HOURS OF

BERLIN, OCT. 23 (AP)-FRIDA HOCKAUF, FAT AND FIFTYISH, IS THE 
FIRST PIN-UP GIRL OF EAST GERMAN COMMUNISM. 

HER DOUBLE-CHINNED COUNTENANCE APPEARS IN LEADING SOVIET ZONE 
NEWSPAPERS UNDER ADORING HEADLINES. THE DRUMS OF PARTY PROPAGANDA 
BEAT IN HER HONOR NIGHT AND DAY. 

YET 4 MONTH AGO SHE WAS PUBLICLY UNKNOWN. WHAT CHANGED THAT 
WASN'T HER SEX APPEAL. IT WAS HER ECONOMIC ALLURE. 

THE "FRIDA HOCKAUF MOVEMENT” HAS SPREAD IN THREE SHORT WEEKS 
THROUGHOUT EAST GERMANY. "HOCKAUF BRIGADES® HAVE BEEN FORMED AMONG 
WOMEN IN STATE INDUSTRIES. "HOCKAUF BRIGADES” HAVE BEEN FORMED AMONG 
WOMEN IN STATE INDUSTRIES. "HOCKAUF BOOKS® ARE BEING PASSED 0 


“THE FRIDA HOCKAUF MOVEMENT” HAS SPREAD IN THREE SHORT WEEKS 
THROUGHOUT EAST GERMANY. "HOCKAUF BOOKS” ARE BEING FORMED AMONG 
WOMEN IN STATE INDUSTRIES. “HOCKAUF BOOKS” ARE BEING PASSED OUT To 
FEMALE WORKERS IN WHICH TO WRITE THEIR “VOLUNTARY® PROMISES TO 
PRODUCE MORE--AT THE SAME WAGE. ; 

FRAU HOCKAUF IS RESPONSIBLE FOR ALL THIS, ACCORDING TO THE RED 
PRESS, BECAUSE SHE SPONTANEOUSLY ANNOUNCED AT A ZITTAU TEXTILE PLANT 
THAT SHE WOULD WEAVE 45 MORE YARDS OF CLOTH THAN HER PRODUCTION 
QUOTA IN THE NEXT THREE MONTHS. 

TWENTY-FOUR HOURS AFTER SHE SPOKE UP, THE PUBLICITY CAMPAIGN GOT 
UNDERWAY. | EIGHTEEN MILLION EAST GERMANS HAVE BEEN LOOKING AT HER 

SKEPTICAL ANTI-COMMUNIST SOURCES HERE AVER THE WHOLE THING WAS 
CAREFULLY PREPARED BY THE SOVIET ZONE GOVERNMENT TO PEP UP ACTIVITY 
IN CONSUMER GOODS INDUSTRIES, WHOSE OUTPUT HAD BEEN LAGGING. 

THE GOVERNMENT, NEARLY TOPPLED BY A REVOLT LAST SUMMER, HAS PROMISED 
TO RAISE THE LIVING STANDARD BUT IS KEEPING DOWN WAGES. {TS HABIT OF 
BOOSTING PRODUCTION QUOTAS WITHOUT BOOSTING PAY WAS A BIG FACTOR IN THE 
JUNE 17 RIOTS BY 2 MILLION WORKERS. 

BACK IN 1943, THE COMMUNISTS UNVEILED A PIN-UP BOY, ADOLF HENNICKE, 
WHO WAS SUDDENLY CREDITED WITH DIGGING MORE COAL DAILY THAN ANY OTHER 
EAST GERMANe HE WAS ACCLAIMED A HERO OF LABOR, GIVEN A DESK JOB, AND 

HENNICKE BRIGADES" SPRANG UP IN ALL HEAVY INDUSTRIES. 

FRAU HOCKAUF , A COMMUNIST PARTY MEMBER FOR 32 YEARS AND MOTHER OF 

A DAUGHTER NOW STUDYING AT THE SOVIET UNIVERSITY OF LENINGRAD, 


IS GETTING HENNICKE'S BUILDUP.

WASHINGTON OCT «23 (AP)-COMMUNIST CHINA HAS SEIZED A 55-YEAR-OLD 

WESTERN CEMETERY IN SHANGHAI “FOR OTHER PURPOSES” AND WILL MOVE ALL 

BODIES INTERRED THERE, THE STATE DEPARTMENT SAID TODAY. 

IN AN ANNOUNCEMENT, THE DEPARTMENT TOLD RELATIVES OF AMERICANS 

BURIED THERE THEY MUST NOTIFY COMMUNIST AUTHORITIES BY OCT.31 IF THEY 

AINS BURIED PRIVATELY IN OTHER SHANGHAI CEMETERIES. 

FERRED REMAINS NOT REMOVED THROUGH INDIVIDUAL ARRANGEMENTS BY 
REPORTEDLY WILL BE REMOVED AT CHINESE COMMUNIST EXPENSE TO 
SECTION OF A CHINESE BURIAL GROUND, NOT NOW CONSECREATED, 

LOCATED SOME 15 MILES NORTH OF SHANGHAI," THE STATE DEPARTMENT 

SAID. 


THE CEMETERY INVOLVED I$ CALLED “BUBBLING WELL CEMETERY® AND 
CONTAINS THE GRAVES OF SOME 195 AMERICANS. MOST OF THE GRAVES THERE 
ARE OF FORMER BRITISH RESIDENTS AND SOME FRENCH. 

AMERICANS WANTING TO ARRANGE FOR REBURIAL WERE ADVISED TO CONSULT 
THE STATE DEPARTMENT'S OFFICE OF SPECIAL COUNSELLOR SERVICES IN 
WASHINGTON FOR INFORMATION AND ASSISTANCE. 

A STATE DEPARTMENT OFFICIALS SAID THE UNITED STATES AND PRESUMABLY 
BRITAIN, WHICH REPRESENTS AMERICAN INTERESTS IN COMMUNIST CHINA, 
WILL ASK FOR MORE TIME FOR RELATIVES TO ARRANGE REBURIAL. THIS 
OFFICIAL ESTIMATED IT WILL COST ABOUT $50 TO PAY FOR REBURIAL. HE

ONE OF THE BITTEREST INDIAN EXPERIENCES IN "NEUTRALISM” HAS COME IN 
THEIR DEALINGS WITH THE 22,400 ANTI-RED CHINESE AND NORTH KOREANS IN 
THEIR CUSTODY. 

THEY HAD HOPED TO SMOOTH THE ARMISTICE PROCEEDINGS BY WINNING THE 
CONFIDENCE OF THESE MEN. BUT THE ANTI-COMMUNISTS PROVED VIOLENT, 
PARTICULARLY THE KOREANS. 

A FEW DAYS AGO, THE INDIAN OFFICER IN CHARGE OF THE CUSTODIAL 
TROOPS, MAJe GENe Se Pe Ps THORAT, WAS ASKED IF HE FELT HIS MEN HAD 
WON THE CONFIDENCE OF THE CAPTIVES. HE THREW BACK HIS ARMS AND 
EXLAIMED, "NO. MY GOD NO." 

INDIAN JUNIOR OFFICERS AT FIRST OPENLY EXPRESSED THE VIEW THAT MANY 
OF THE CHINESE AND NORTH KOREANS WOULD GO BACK TO THE REDS. 

IT WAS SOMETHING OF A SHOCK TO THE INDIANS WHEN AFTER TWO DAYS OF 
ACTUAL EXPLANATIONS SESSIONS, ONLY 19 CHINESE CHOSE TO RETURN, OF THE 
921 WHO ATTENDED EXPLANATIONS. 

THE INDIANS STILL REGARD THE PRISONERS AS WAYWARD CHILDREN. INDIAN 
QFFICERS ARE APT TO GIVE ORDERS SUCH AS "COME ALONG YOU CHAPS," OR 
PLEASE, PLEASE WS. | 

ODDLY ENOUGH, THE INDIAN SYSTEM SEEMS TO WORK AS WELL AS ANY. 

THE PRISONERS HAVE SHOWN A CERTAIN RESPECT FOR THE STAUNCH 
DISCIPLINE OF THE INDIAN REGULARS--DRAWN FROM FIVE PROUD AND COLORFUL 
REGIMENTS--THE DOGRAS, JATS, MAHRATTAS, GARHWALIS AND RAJPUTANA

RUSSIA WAS BOYCOTTING THE COUNCIL WHEN IT TOOK ITS DECISION TO USE 
FORCE AGAINST THE COMMUNIST INVADERS OF SOUTH KOREA, BUT RETURNED A 
SHORT TIME LATER TO BLOCK ALL FURTHER ACTION. THE KOREAN ISSUE THEN WAS 
QUICKLY TRANSFERRED TO THE ASSEMBLY, WHERE IT HAS REMAINED EVER SINCE. 
THIS LED TO THE ACHESON PLAN, WHICH DEAN ACHESON, THEN THE U.S. 
SECRETARY OF STATE, SUBMITTED IN THE FALL OF 1950 TO GIVE THE ASSEMBLY 
MORE FLEXIBILITY IN DEALING WITH SUDDEN DISPUTES. ONE PROVISIONS OF THE 
PLAN, AS APPROVED, MADE IT POSSIBLE FOR THE ASSEMBLY TO BE CALLED INTO 
EMERGENCY SESSION WITHIN 24 HOURS.

TQK¥O, OCT. 26 (AP)-REPRESENTATIVES OF JAPAN, COMMONWEALTH COUNTRIES 
AND THE U.N. COMMAND TODAY SIGNED AN AGREEMENT GIVING JAPAN JURISDICTION 
OVER UNC. SOLDIERS WHO COMMIT CRIMES WHILE OFF DUTY. 

THE AGREEMENT WAS SIMILAR TO ONE SIGNED EARLIER GIVING JAPAN JURIS- 
DICTION OVER AMERICAN SECURITY TROOPS FOR OFF-DUTY CRIMES. 

IT APPLIES TO TROOPS OF ALL UNC FORCES WHO ARE EITHER STATIONED IN 


JAPAN OR COME HERE ON LEAVE FROM KOREA. 
THE INDIVIDUAL NATIONS OF THE UNC WILL HAVE JURISDICTION OVER SOLD- 


IERS WHO COMMIT CRIMES WHILE ON DUTY. 

THE AGREEMENT FOR JURISDICTION OF U.N. SOLDIERS GOES INTO EFFECT 
THURSDAY,. THE SAME DAY THAT THE AGREEMENT SIGNED LAST MONTH BETWEEN

B GERMANY, OCT.26 (AP)-WEST GERMANY'S MOUNTING IMPATIENCE WITH 
THE LONG DELAY IN CREATING THE EUROP ENSE. COMMUNITY EDC) AND 
STORING GERMAN INDEPENDENCE-COULD FORCE THE UNITED STATES TO RECAST 
[TS LONG-TERM EUROPEAN POLICY NEXT YEAR. 

THIS IS THE OPINION OF RESPONSIBLE ALLIED OFFICIALS WHO SAID HERE 
TODAY THAT GERMAN PUBLIC OPINION 1S BECOMING INCREASINGLY RESTLESS 
OVER THE FAILURE: TO SETTLE THE NATION'S POLITICAL AND MILITARY ROLE IN 
THE FREE WORLD. 

UNLESS DEFINITE ACTION IS TAKEN SOON BY OTHER WESTERN EUROPEAN 
COUNTRIES TO RATIFY THE TWIN TREATIES DESIGNED TO ORGANIZE THE EDC AND 
END THE LONG ALLIED OCCUPATION OF GERMANY, THESE ALLIED OFFICIALS FEAR 
CHANCELLOR KONRAD ADENAUER MAY BE FORCED to SEEK AN ALTERNATIVE WAY TO 
WIN SOVEREIGNTY AND REARM WEST GERMANY. 

THE EDC TREATY AND THE ALLIED-WEST GERMAN PEACE CONTRACT 
SIGNED IN MAY, 1952, WOULD GIVE WEST GERMANY HER FREEDOM AND CREATE 
A POWERFUL SIX-NATION EUROPEAN ARMY TO INCLUDE 500,000 GERMAN TROOPS. 

THE TWIN TREATIES ARE CORNERSTONES OF AN AMERICAN PROGRAM TO MAKE 
WESTERN EUROPE INTO A SINGLE DEFENSE AND POLITICAL COMMUNITY CAPABLE oO} 
DEFENDING AND SU ! é

SUBSTITUTE FOR EDC AND A NEW FORMULA FOR GIVING WEST GERMANY HER 
FREEDOM INSIDE THE WESTERN COMMUNITY WILL FALL ON THE UNITED STATES, IN 
THE OPINION OF THE OFFICIALS HERE. : 

MANY OFFICIALS FEAR THE FAILURE OF EDC WOULD WRECK THE NORTH 
ATLANTIC ALLIANCE, WITH FRANCE REFUSING TO PERMIT DIRECT GERMAN 
MEMBERSHIP IN THE NORTH ATLANTIC TREATY ORGANIZATION (NATO) AND THE 
UNITED STATES INSISTING ON THE REARMAMENT OF WEST GERMANY,

JAPANESE DEFENSE 

BY JOHN Me HIGHTOWER 

WAGHENGTON, OCT. 26 (AP)-STATE DERARITMENT OFFICIALS HOPE TO CON- 
CLUDE THIS WEEK A MILITARY AID ARRANGEMENT PROVIDING. U. S. SUPPORT 
FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF A RELATIVELY MODEST JAPANESE DEFENSE FORCE. 

INFORMATION AVAILABLE ON THE PROGRESS OF NEGOTIATION FAR 

INDICATES THAT IN THE END NEITHER SIDE WILL GET ALL IT WANTS? 
(1) JAPAN WILL NOT GET A LARGE SCALE, LONG TERM ECONOMIC AID 

(2) THE UNITED STATES WILL NOT GET ASSURANCE OF AS LARGE 
A DEFENSE FORCE AS IT WOULD LIKE TO SEE IN JAPAN. 

NEVERTHELESS. ‘INFORMANTS SAID TODAY THE TALKS HAVE BASICALLY BEEN 
SATISFACTORY ANB, DISCOUNTING THE MAXIMUM DESIRES OF BOTH SIDES 
SHOULD RESULT IN’SUBSTANTIALLY INCREASING FAR EASTERN SECURITY AND 
EVENTUALLY. AKING SOME OF THE LOAD THERE OFF THE UNITED STATES. 

THE T BAS OPENED HERE OCT. 2 WITH HAYATO IKEDA, PERSONAL REPRE- 
SENTATI!&lt; OF PREMIER. SHIGERU YOSHIDA THE CHIEF JAPANESE NEGO- 
TIATORs MEANWHILE, DISCUSSIONS TOWARD FORMAL MUTUAL SECURITY PACT 
HAVE BEF GOING ONIN TOKYO. THE TOKYO TALKS WERE DESCRIBED AS 
BEING Cl ‘CERNED WITH TECHNICAL PROVISIONS OF THE PACT; THOSE IN 
WASHINGTON WITH MAJOR POLICY DECISIONS. 

SECRETARY -OF STATE DULLES, CHIEF-ARCHITECT OF -THE-JAPANESE 
PEACE TREATY WHO HAS LONG CONTENDED JAPAN SHOULD ARM IN ITS OWN 
DEFENSE. SAID SOME TIME AGO HE THOUGHT THE JAPANESE DEFENSE FORCE 
COULD RUN AROUND 300,000 TO 350,000 MEN. MORE RECENTLY, FORMER 
JAPANESE PREMIER HITOSHI ASHIDA SAID ON A VISIT TO THIS COUNTRY HE 
FORESAW 15 GROUND DIVIDIONS OF 290,000 MEN PLUS A 4,000 PLANE AIR 
FORCE AND 300,000 TONS OF SMALL NAVAL CRAFT. 

PERSONS FAMILIAR WITH THE TALKS BETWEEN IKEDA AND ASST. SECRETARY 
OF STATE WALTER Se ROBERTSON SAID IKEDA HAS INDICATED THAT WITH 
THE SCALE OF AID OFFERED BY WASHINGTON HIS GOVERNMENT WILL BE ABLE 
TO DO SUBSTANTIALLY LESS THAN DULLES AND ASHIDA INDICATED. 

ONE SPECULATION IS THAT THE NEGOTIATIONS MAY END WITH AN AGREEMENT 
ROUGHLY TO DOUBLE THE PRESENT NATIONAL SECURITY FORCE OF 110,000 MEN, 
APART FROM SMALL AIR AND NAVAL FORCES. 

AUTHORITIES REPRESENTED THE Us Se AS FAVORING DEVELOPMENT OF WHAT 
THEY CALLED A “RELATIVELY MODEST DEFENSE FORCE” OF GROUND, SEA AND 
AIR UNITS WHICH WOULD BE STRICTLY DEFENSIVE IN CHARACTER. 

IKEDA IS REPORTED TO HAVE COME SEEKING U. $. COMMITMENTS OF 
EXTENSIVE ECONOMIC AS WELL AS MILITARY AID. THE UNITED STATES HAS 
NOT HAD AN ECONOMIC AID PROGRAM FOR JAPAN FOR SEVERAL YEARS. IN- 
FORMANTS SAID PRIVATELY THIS POLICY WOULD CONTINUE.

RARIS, OCT 27 (AP)-EX-PREMIER EDOUARD DALADIER DECLARED TODAY 
FRANCE SHOULD TELL THE COMMUNIST-LED REBELS IN INDOCHINAS "WE OFFER“ , 
YOU PEACE. DO YOU WANT IT?" 

| DALADIER SPOKE IN A NATIQNAL ASSEMBLY DEBATE ON THE HOPES AND AIMS 

Mm OF FRANCE IN PURSUING THE SEVEN-YEAR WAR THAT HAS SIPHONED OFF FRENCH 
RESOURCES AND MANPOWER IN EVER-INCREASING QUANTITIES. 

DEPUTY AFTER DEPUTY MOUNTED THE ROSTRUM TO DEMAND WHAT PLANS THE 
GOVERNMENT HAS TO END THE DRAINe MANY SPOKE OF NEGOTIATION--WITH 
VIETMINH LEADER HO CHI MINH OR OTHER COMMUNIST CHIEFS. 

DALADIER, A RADICAL SOCIALIST, ALSO DECLARED HIMSELF AN ADVOCATE 
OF A FIVE-POWER CONFERENCE IN WHICH RED CHINA WOULD PARTICIPATE. HE 
ADDED, HOWEVER, THAT HE DID NOT MUCH BELIEVE IT COULD BE ARRANGED. 

"WHEN GREAT BRITAIN RECOGNIZED CHINA," HE SAID, "WE DID NOTHINGs 
WAS IT OUT OF SERVILITY OR KINDNESS TO THE UNITED STATES?" 

WHEN DALADIER REMARKED THAT AN OPEN OFFER OF PEACE SHOULD BE MADE, 
ONE DEPUTY FROM THE RANKS OF THE POPULAR REPUBLICAN MOVEMENT (MRP) 
SHOUTED "MUNICH! MUNICH!" THIS WAS A REFERENCE TO THE FACT DALADIER 
WENT WITH BRITISH PRIME MINISTER NEVILLE CHAMBERLAIN TO ARRANGE THE 
MUNICH PEACE WITH HITLER. 

DALADIER, UNRUFFLED, RETORTED: "STOP CROACKING. I CAN SHOW YoU 
SOME ARTICLES FROM THAT PERIOD WHERE GEORGES BIDAULT AND FRANCISQUE 
GAY (MEMBERS OF THE MRP) WERE WARM PARTISANS OF MUNICH." 

MEANWHILE, PARIS SOURCES SAID THE UNITED STATES HAS ALMOST LENT A 
HAND--AND MAY YET--TO STRENGTHEN THE POSITION OF PREMIER JOSEPH 
LANIEL'S GOVERNMENT ON INDOCHINA.

HAD BEEN PROJECTED FOR.A DECLARATION OF FULL SUPPORT OF THE FRENCH 
UNION THROUGH A PUBLIC STATEMENT BY SECRETARY OF STATE DULLES. THE 
THREE ASSOCIATED STATES OF INDOCHINA=-VIET NAM, LAOS AND CAMBODIA-~ARE 


% LINKED TO FRANCE IN THIS UNION. 


OTHER SOURCES SAID THE PUBLIC STATEMENT HAS BEEN WITHHELD, BUT THE 
IDEA OF AMERICAN ENDORSEMENT OF THE FRENCH UNION DEFINITELY IS NOT 
DEAD.

MM cTRUCTURE OF THE FRENCH UNION, SAYING IN A RECENT SPEECH THAT ITS 
FLEXIBILITY OFFERS TRUE FREEDOM FOR ALL ITS MEMBERS.

BY RUSSELL BRINES 19 

EN ROUTE_WITH NIXON, OCT. 28 RICHARDUAIXON 
WALKED ON THE BRINK OF A POLITICAL VOLCANO ON“HIS THREE-DAY VISIT TO 
INDONESIA. HE MAY HAVE EASED POLITICAL TENSIONS--OR ADDED FUFL TO A 
POTENTIAL EXPLOSION. 

THE NEXT FEW WEEKS WILL TELL. 

NIXON'S OFFICIAL CALL ON THIS RICH ISLAND REPUBLIC UNEQUESTIONABLY 
BROUGHT TEMPORARY CALM. BUT VETERAN OBSERVERS SAY IT WILL BE SEVERAL 
WEEKS BEFORE THE ULTIMATE RESULTS ARE EVIDENT. 

MANY EXPERIENCED FOREIGN AND INDONESIAN OBSERVERS SAY A BLOW-UP IS 
COMING SOON. 

THE GOVERNMENT OF PRESIDENT SUKARNO IS FIGHTING FOUR MAJOR MILITARY 
CAMPAIGNS AGAINST ASSORTED ENEMIES, WITH INTENSIFIED OPERATIONS _ 
IMMINENT 

SIMULTANEOUSLY, A TENSE POLITICAL BATTLE IS BUILDING UP BENEATH THE 
SURFACE AND SUKARNO FACES INTENSIFIED MOSLEM OPPOSITION. 

SUKARNO, LONG AN OPPORTUNIST, HAS ACCEPTED COMMUNIST AND LEFTIST 
SUPPORT. HE HAS A SUSPECTED COMMUNIST AS A WAR MINISTER AND A KNOWN 
LEFTIST IN THE POWERFUL POST OF JUSTICE MINISTER. 

ONE RESULT HAS BEEN A CLEAR WARNING THAT CENSORSHIP MAY BE CLAMPED 

A WARNING SO PLAIN THAT THIS STORY WAS BEING FILED 
OUTSIDE THE COUNTRY. 


AGAINST THIS BACKGROUND, NIXON MADE AN OBVIOUS ATTEMPT TO BUILD UP 
SUKARNO PERSONALLY DURING A VISIT THAT LIMITED PUBLIC APPEARANCES TO 
SIGHTSEEING AND SOCIAL ENGAGEMENTS. | 

OBSERVERS SAY THE BEST RESULTS, FROM THE AMERICAN VIEWPOINT. COULD

SECRET, BUT LEAKS WERE INEVITABLE--IN PERHAPS A GARBLED VERSION.

THE QUESTION OF WHETHER INDONESIA FACES INTENSIFIED POLITICAL AND 
MILITARY STRIFE OR WHETHER, FOR THE PRESENT, THE PROBLEM CAN-BE SOLVED 
BY ORIENTAL COMPROMISE. 

WHILE NIXON WAS IN THE COUNTRY, THE GOVERNMENT MOVED TANKS AND 
TROOP REINFORCEMENTS TO NORTHERN SUMATRA FOR INTENSIFIED ACTION AGAINST

COMMUNICATION LINES ON THIS RICH ISLAND, WHICH THE DUTCH FOUGHT FOR 30 
YEARS TO SUBDUE.

BANDS. BATTLING PARTLY FOR WARLORD CONTROL, PROBABLY WILL IGNORE THE

ADVANCE) NEW YORK, OCT. 28 (AP)=SIR ALEXANDER GRANTHAM, GOVERNOR 
OF HONG KONG, PREDICTED IN AN INTERVIEW PUBLISHED TODAY THAT THE 
RLD WILL BENEFIT IN TRADE WITH COMMUNIST CHINA WHEN, AND IF, THE 
UNITED NATIONS TRADE EMBARGO IS LIFTED. 
IN AN INTERVIEW PUBLISHED IN NEWSWEEK MAGAZINE, GRANTHAM SAID THAT 
IF THERE IS PEACE WITH CHINA AND THE EMBARGO IS LIFTED "I ANTICIPATE 
THAT THE CHINESE COMMUNISTS WILL NOT ONLY BE WILLING TO DO BUSINESS 
WITH THE WEST BUT WILL ALSO WANT TO DO SOt POLITICALLY, BECAUSE CHINA 
WON'T WANT TO RELY TOO MUCH ON ONE POWER, RUSSIA, AND PRACTICALLY 
BECAUSE RUSSIA WILL NOT BE ABLE TO SUPPLY CHINA WITH ALL SHE NEEDS." 
"THE POTENTIAL FOR TRADE BETWEEN CHINA AND THE REST OF THE WORLD'S _ 
IMMENSE," GRANTHAM CONTINUED. “TO DEVELOP HERSELF CHINA WILL NEED MUCH 
CAPITAL EQUIPMENT FOR MANY YEARS TO COME. THE COUNTRIES WHICH CAN BEST 
SUPPLY HER ARE THE INDUSTRIAL COUNTRIES OF THE FREE WORLD, NOTABLY THE 
UNITED KINGDOM, UNITED STATES, AND GERMANY. JAPAN, WHICH HAS THE 
ADVANTAGE. OF PROXIMITY, WILL ALSO BE ABLE TO ASSIST, BUT TO A LESSER 


EXTENT. 


" 

THERE WILL ALSO BE OTHER TRADE IN WHICH ASIAN AND OTHER COUNTRIES 
WILL SHARE. IF CHINA OPENS HERSELF UP TO TRADE WITH THE FREE WORLD, 
ALL WILL BENEFIT, BUT MOST OF ALL CHINA HERSELF." 

GRANTHAM SAID THERE WAS A VERY SERIOUS BUSINESS RECESSION IN 
HONG KONG DUE TO THE EMBARGO AND THAT HONG KONG BUSINESSMEN QUESTION 
WHETHER THE EMBARGO HAS DONE MUCH TO CURTAIL CHINA’S WAR POTENTIAL. 

HE ADDED, IN RESPONSE TO A QUESTION, THAT "HONG KONG CAN SURVIVE 
IITHOUT CHINA, BUT FROM HER GEOGRAPHICAL SITUATION ON THE FRINGE OF 
CHINA, CHINA ts INEVITABLY HER MAJOR TRADING PARTNER. TRADE WITH 
OTHER ASIAN COUNTRIES HAS DEVELOPED, BUT THEY CAN NEVER TAKE THE PLACE 


ENTIRELY OF CHINA."

THE EDC TREATY. WHICH WILL PERMIT THE REARMING OF WEST GERMANY AND 
POOL SOLDIERS FROM WEST GERMANY, ITALY, FRANCE, BELGIUM, THE 
NETHERLANDS AND LUXEMBOURG IN A°’UNIFIED COMMAND, WAS SIGNED MAY 27 
1952. SO FAR IT HAS BEEN RATIFIED ONLY BY WEST GERMANY AND ONE HOUSE 
OF THE DUTCH PARLIAMENT. 

THE QUESTION OF RATIFICATION WAS NOT BEFORE THE COUNCIL OF THE 
REPUBLIC. THE TREATY HAS NOT YET BEEN PUT TO PARLIAMENT FORMALLY BY 
THE FRENCH CABINET. NO ACTION IS EXPECTED BEFORE THE NEW YEAR AND 
POSSIBLY LATE SPRING. 


IDEA. THE EUROPEAN ARMY PROJECT WAS CONCEIVED AND NEGOTIATED BY HIS 
PREDECESSOR AS FOREIGN MINISTER, ROBERT SCHUMAN. 

THE COUNCIL OF THE REPUBLIC REFUSED TO APPROVE A SOCIALIST RESOLU- 
TION WHICH EXPRESSED APPROVAL FOR THE PRINCIPLE BUT LISTED SPECIFIC 
OBJECTIONS. INSTEAD, THE MAJORITY RALLIED AROUND THE INNOCUOUS STATE- 
MENT. BUT WHEN THE TREATY COMES UP FOR RATIFICATION THE VOTING LINEUP 
IS BOUND TO BE DIFFERENT. 

SENATORS WHO WERE ELECTED UNDER THE LEADERSHIP OF GEN. CHARLES DE 
GAULLE VOTED FOR THE RESOLUTION TODAY. BUT NO ONE EXPECTS THE GAULLISTS 
TO APPROVE WHEN IT COMES TIME FOR RATIFICATION. 

THE SOCIALISTS VOTED AGAINST THE RESOLUTION TODAY, BUT THEY 
PROBABLY WILL BE IN THE OTHER COLUMN IN THE RATIFICATION TEST. 

THE COUNCIL OF THE REPUBLIC VOTING LINEUP CANNOT BE TAKEN AS A GUIDE 
FOR WHAT MIGHT HAPPEN IN THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY. SOCIALIST SENATORS 
SHOWED MORE ENTHUSIASM FOR THE TREATY THAN HAVE THE SOCIALIST DEPUTIES. 
ON THE OTHER HAND, THE PROJECT GOT LESS SUPPORT FROM SOME CENTRIST 
PARTIES IN THE COUNCIL THAN IS EXPECTED IN THE ASSEMBLY.

ROME, OCT. 31 (AP)-THE DELAY OF TWO TANKERS BOUND FOR YUGOSLAVIA 
WITH CARGOES OF GASOLINE PROMPTED REPORTS TODAY THAT ITALY HAS BANNED 
OIL EXPORTS TO THE NEIGHBOR WITH WHOM SHE IS QUARRELLING OVER TRIESTE. 

SOURCES IN NAPLES AND BARI SAID THE CLAMP-DOWN ON SAILING OF THE 
TWO SHIPS CAME ON ORDERS OF ITALIAN GOVERNMENT. IN ROME, HOWEVER 
THE GOVERNMENT DECLINED COMMENT. YUGOPRESS, SEMI-OFFICIAL NEWS AGENCY 
IN BELGRADE, REPORTED LAST NIGHT THAT ITALY HAS BARRED ALL OIL EXPORTS 

HELD IN NAPLES IS THE TANKER DUCHESS, WITH A PANAMA REGISTRY AND A 
GREEK CREW. IT IS OWNED BY THE VIVALET COMPANY OF PANAMA CITY. 

PORT POLICE SAID THE MINISTRY OF FOREIGN TRADE ORDERED THE SHIP'S 
DELAY. THE COMPANY'S AGENT IN NAPLES, OSCAR COSULICH, SAID 

CUSTOMS OFFICIALS HAVE ORDERED THE DUCHESS' 7,000-TON GASOLINE CARGO 
UNLOADED BUT THAT THE UNLOADING HAS NOT YET BEGUN. A REPRESENTATIVE 
OF THE SOCONY VACUUM OIL COMPANY SAID HIS CONCERN HAD LOADED THE 
FUEL ON THE DUCHESS ON ORDERS FROM NEW YORK. 

HELD IN THE SOUTHERN ADRIATIC PORT OF BARI IS THE ITALIAN TANKER: 
PARAGGI, WITH A CARGO OF 1,000 TONS OF GASOLINE DESTINED FOR THE 
YUGOSLAV PORTS OF DUBROVNIK AND SPLIT. SOURCES AT THE BARI PORT 
SAID THE CARGO HAD NOT BEEN SEQUESTERED, BUT THAT THE SHIP WAS 
PREVENTED FROM SAILING FOR YUGOSLAVIA ON ORDERS OF THE TRADE 
MINISTRY. PORT AUTHORITIES DECLINED COMMENT.

BERLIN, OCT. 31 (AP)-THE EAST GERMAN COMMUNIST GOVERNMENT CLAIMED 
TODAY THAT LARGE ESPIONAGE, SABOTAGE AND TERROR GROUPS OPERATING 
UNDER U.S» GUIDANCE IN THE SOVIET ZONE HAVE BEEN WRECKED WITHIN THE 
ARRESTS WERE MADE IN EAST BERLIN, AT HALLE, COTTBUS, POTSDAM AND

IT CLAIMED ALSO THAT RADIO TRANSMITTERS OF AMERICAN ORIGIN, WEAPONS 


AND “SECRET INSTRUCTIONS” HAVE BEEN CONFISCATED. 
THE ARRESTED PERSONS, WHOSE NUMBER WAS NOT REVEALED, WERE 
DESCRIBED AS AGENTS OF tHE AMERICAN AND THE WEST GERMAN SECRET 


SERVICE. THE EAST GERMAN MINISTRY ASSERTED THEY RECEIVED THEIR ORDERS 
OUT OF WEST GERMANY AND WEST BERLIN "FROM THE SAME PEOPLE WHO PREPARED 
AND STAGED THE FASCIST PUTSCH OF JUNE 17." 

IN THE PAST SIX WEEKS, EAST GERMAN COURTS HAVE IMPOSED 2 DEATH AND 
3 LIFE IMPRISONMENT SENTENCES ON DEFENDANTS TRIED ON SIMILAR CHARGES. 
TWENTY OTHERS WERE SENT TO PRISON FOR A TOTAL OF 205 YEARS. 

FOUR EAST GERMANS WERE CONVICTED TODAY AS "ECONOMIC SPIES” AND 
SENTENCED TO PRISON TERMS RANGING FROM 5 TO 14 YEARS.

THE INFORMATION TO THE WEST BERLIN "FREE JURISTS COMMITTEE." oy

WORKERS REVOLT OF JUNE 17.

BY EDMOND LEBRETON 
WASHINGTON, OCT. 31 (AP)-THE MARSHALL PLAN FOR BRINGING WAR-SHAT- 
TERED EUROPE BACK TO ECONOMIC LIFE IS PASSING INTO HISTORY AS GEN. 


GEORGE Ce. MARSHALL*®S NAME GOES ON THE ENDURING ROLL OF NOBEL PEACE 


PRIZE WINNERS. 
FREE EUROPE, DESPITE SOME DISAPPOINTMENTS AND RELAPSES, HAS MADE 
A TREMENDOUS RECOVERY. ECONOMIC AID FROM THE UNITED STATES HAS 
DWINDLED FROM A MULTI-BILLION DOLLAR FLOOD TO A RELATIVE TRICKLE 
THAT SEEMS DESTINED SOON TO DRY UP ALTOGETHER. THE EMPHASIS NOW IS 
ON "TRADE--NOT AID." 


IT WAS IN MANY RESPECTS A DIFFERENT WORLD WHICH HEARD SECRETARY OF 


‘STATE A COMMENCEMENT ADDRESS AT HARVARD UNIVERSITY 


JUNE 5, 1947, PROPOSE THE PLAN WHICH IMMEDIATELY TOOK HIS NAME. 

HE CALLED’FOR AN OUTPOURING OF GIFTS AND LOANS TO RESTORE PRODUC- 
TION AND EMPLOYMENT IN COUNTRIES THREATENED WITH COLLAPSE. IT WAS 
AN EFFORT LATER CALLED BY A BRITISH CHANCELLOR OF THE EXCHEQUER 
| oF THE MOST--IF NOT THE MOST--GENEROUS, MAGNANIMOUS ACTS IN 

ORY. . 

“ITS SUPPORTERS HAVE ALSO CALLED IT A WISE AMERICAN POLICY, BLOCKING 
ANY TAKE-OVER BY COMMUNISTS IN MAJOR WESTERN EUROPEAN COUNTRIES AND 
PROVIDING THE UNITED STATES WITH SINEWY ALLIES. ITS CRITICS CALLED IT 
A GIANT GIVE-AWAY WHICH DRAINED AMERICAN RESOURCES WITHOUT ACHIEVING 
WORLD PROSPERITY. 

PRESIDENT TRUMAN SUBMITTED THE PLAN TO CONGRESS AS A 17 BILLION 
DOLLAR PROGRAM TO EXTEND TO MID-1952. BUT CONGRESS ENACTED A SHORT- 
RANGE AUTHORIZING LAW THE FOLLOWING APRIL, AND STARTED AID TO 19

CONFERENCE. CZECHOSLOVAKIA, THEN NOT COMPLETELY UNDER THE RUSSIAN 
THUMB, ACCEPTED AND THEN WITHDREW UNDER MOSCOW ORDERS. A FEW WEEKS 
LATER THE COMMUNISTS TOOK OVER CZECHOSLOVAKIA. 

THE ECONOMIC COOPERATION ADMINISTRATION (ECA), SET UP TO ADMINISTER 
THE AID, WAS STAFFED LARGELY BY BUSINESSMEN AND HEADED BY PAUL G. 

OFFMAN, AN AUTOMOB x 2 

ECA CLAIMED A TELLING EFFECT IN EUROPE FROM THE START OF THE 
PROGRAM, AND IT WAS CREDITED WITH A POLITICAL VICTORY--DEFEAT OF THE 
COMMUNISTS IN ITALIAN ELECTIONS--IN THE FIRST MONTH OF ITS LIFE. :
